https://kloop.kg/blog/2026/10/21/aspekov.body: Facebook Twitter VK Telegram WhatsApp Казахский оппозиционер Мухтар Аблязов * и кыргызский президент Садыр Жапаров продолжают свой обмен мнениями через сторонних лиц. Ранее, 17 октября, Аблязов в эфире политдвижения «Шумкар» * , деятельность которого в Кыргызстане объявили «экстремистской», рассказал, что в 2020 году говорил 40 минут с Садыром Жапаровым и что вышедший в ту пору из колонии политик искал финансирование. Затем через издание Super.kg кыргызский президент ответил Аблязову, во-первых, признав, что смотрел видео «Шумкара», во-вторых, признав разговор с казахским оппозиционером. Президент заявил, что разговор был уложен в две минуты, трубку ему передал его сторонник Мелис Аспеков * . Жапаров сказал, что «нелогично просить денег у нищего», опровергнув информацию о том, что мог искать финансирование через или у Аблязова. И Аблязов, и Жапаров совпали в одном — что казахский оппозиционер хотел попасть в Казахстан через Бишкек. Однако Аблязов настаивает, что после разговора с Жапаровым решил не иметь с ним дела. Жапаров настаивает, что сам не хотел приезда Аблязова в Кыргызстан, чтобы не портить отношения с соседями. Аблязова он назвал аферистом. И сказал, что ему дал кыргызский паспорт бывший президент Алмазбек Атамбаев. 20 октября Аблязов ответил Жапарову — снова через эфир «Шумкара». Он обвинил Жапарова во лжи, однако подтвердил какие-то детали, которые называл Жапаров — например, коммуникацию через Мелиса Аспекова. Аблязов настаивает — информация кыргызского президента о наличии у казахского оппозиционера кыргызского паспорта лжива. «Ложь про паспорт. Никакой паспорт мне Атамбаев не выписывал», — говорит Аблязов. Также он говорит, что Жапаров якобы поддерживал его планы по свержению власти в Казахстане. «Когда я выразил удивление, что он из тюрьмы смог прийти к власти, он сказал так «И у вас так будет. Вы тоже победите». То есть он поддерживал мои планы по свержению режима в Казахстане и не было такого, чтобы он говорил «не приезжайте, я не хочу испортить отношения с Казахстаном». Все это ложь [...] Его помощник, по приказу Садыра Жапарова, хотел мне помочь организовать революцию в Казахстане. И мы все эти вещи обсуждали», — настаивает Аблязов. Под помощником Аблязов очевидно имеет в виду бывшего сторонника Жапарова Мелиса Аспекова, который сейчас находится в заключении. Аспекова упоминают и Жапаров, и Аблязов. «Мелис Аспеков начал со мной обсуждать их будущие планы, намеревался приехать. И он же мне сказал, что в ГКНБ сидят агенты ФСБ, что фактически контролируется Россией Кыргызстан. Потому что когда я завел речь, что Казахстан выйдет из ЕАЭС, Садыр Жапаров перепугался и быстро свернул разговор», — говорит Аблязов. На это заявление Аблязова на момент выпуска материала Садыр Жапаров еще не отреагировал. *Мухтар Аблязов — опальный казахский политик, бывший владелец БТА Банка, бывший министр энергетики, который сейчас проживает во Франции. В 2001 году Аблязов стал одним из основателей оппозиционного движения «Демократический выбор Казахстана», которое в Казахстане признали экстремистским. Казахские суды заочно приговорили Аблязова к 20 годам лишения свободы. В 2016 году Аблязов заявил, что финансировал кыргызскую революцию 2005 года. *Мелис Аспеков — бывший сторонник Садыра Жапарова. В марте 2024 суд признал его виновным по делу о приготовлении массовых беспорядков и приговорил к семи годам лишения свободы. Уже будучи в заключении, он записал несколько видеообращений, в которых рассказал как Жапаров в 2020 году якобы взял $1 млн у экс-президента Сооронбая Жээнбекова на «организацию предвыборного штаба» для участия в гонке за президентское кресло. По словам Аспекова, он также получил $3 млн у осужденного за коррупцию экс-зампреда таможни Райымбека Матраимова, которые тот якобы передал Жапарову «для организации анти-митинга 9 октября 2020 года». *«Шумкар» — политдвижение, в которое входят критики правления Жапарова эколог Самат Кушбек, политаналитик Айдар Раев, бывший внешний управляющий «Кумтором» Тенгиз Болтурук и политблогер Сыргак Кенжебаев. Власти Кыргызстана признали экстремистской «деятельность организаций в лице» этих людей, но не признали их самих экстремистами. Также кыргызские правоохранители задержали Сыргака Кенжебаева во Вьетнаме — его обвиняют в призывах к массовым беспорядкам и мошенничестве. Суд отправил Кенжебаева на месяц в СИЗО. А в соцсетях распространяли фейковое фото задержания Самата Кушбека — что оказалось неправдой, информацию 20 октября опроверг сам эколог, выйдя в эфир «Шумкара». ЭТО МОЖЕТ БЫТЬ ИНТЕРЕСНО ЕЩЕ ОТ АВТОРА «Нелогично просить денег у нищего». Жапаров отрицает, что обращался за финансами к казахскому оппозиционеру Аблязову Сыргак Кенжебаев намерен баллотироваться в президенты В Кыргызстане признали экстремистской деятельность оппозиционного движения «Шумкар» — туда входят Кенжебаев и Болтурук

https://www.amnesty.org/ru/latest/news/2.body: Комментируя сообщения о задержании всё большего числа мирных активистов, протестовавших против запрета на ношение хиджаба в школах, а также исчезновении активиста, который пытался организовать бесплатные онлайн-занятия для девочек, затронутых новыми правилами ношения школьной формы, директор Amnesty International по Восточной Европе и Центральной Азии Мари Стразерс заявила: «Массовые задержания мирных протестующих наряду с участниками насильственных беспорядков, в том числе, по сообщениям, матери, протестовавшей против отстранения дочери от занятий, а также исчезновение активиста, который хотел помочь девочкам, затронутым новыми ограничениями, — характерное проявление насильственного подавления государством законного осуществления права на мирные протесты и преследования за свободу выражения мнений и любое инакомыслие в Азербайджане. Не допускать девочек в классы из-за того, что они носят хиджаб, — дискриминация, нарушающая их право на образование, а также свободу религии и выражения мнений. Светский характер государственного образования не оправдывает всеобщий запрет на религиозную одежду. Не допускать девочек в классы из-за того, что они носят хиджаб, — дискриминация, нарушающая их право на образование, а также свободу религии и выражения мнений Мари Стразерс, директор Amnesty International по Восточной Европе и Центральной Азии Власти Азербайджана должны отменить эти дискриминационные ограничения и обеспечить возвращение в школы затронутых ими учениц и учителей. Они должны немедленно и безоговорочно освободить всех, кого задержали исключительно за мирное осуществление своих прав. Власти обязаны уважать право на мирные протесты и все права человека». Справка Согласно новым правилам о школьной форме, с 12 октября учеников и учителей в хиджабах перестали допускать в школы по всему Азербайджану. Это вызвало массовые протесты и акции гражданского неповиновения, некоторые из которых сопровождались насилием. По данным МВД, в тот день только в Баку задержали 37 человек, тогда как активисты сообщали о более чем 200 задержанных. В то же время пользователи сообщали, что в Азербайджане стали недоступны TikTok и Instagram. Большинство задержанных вскоре отпустили, однако неизвестно, сколько человек остаются под стражей. Среди известных случаев — Гудрат Абдуллаев, которого за публикацию в TikTok подвергли административному аресту на 25 суток, и Рафаэль Гусейнзаде, задержанный на 30 суток после того, как написал на здании школы «Свободу хиджабу!». Тринадцатого октября по подозрению в попытке поджога школы задержали шестерых несовершеннолетних. По статье 233 Уголовного кодекса, предусматривающей ответственность за организацию действий, нарушающих общественный порядок, или активное участие в них, было возбуждено уголовное дело. Официально в связи с этим делом пока никого не арестовали. Четырнадцатого октября мусульманский активист Ага Гусейнов сообщил об аресте своей жены Шахизяр Гусейновой. Днём ранее её задержали после того, как она вышла на протест у школы в Баку: их дочь не допустили к занятиям. По словам Гусейнова, его жена помещена под стражу на срок четыре месяца, однако ему не сообщили, в чём её обвиняют. Илькин Гусейнов, активист, запустивший бесплатную онлайн-платформу, которая связывала учителей-волонтёров с детьми, отстранёнными от занятий, в том числе из-за ношения хиджаба, пропал 14 октября. Перед этим он вышел из дома в Баку в сопровождении неизвестных.

https://www.rferl.org/a/iran-pakistan-ba.body: Features The Landscape Of Militancy In The Iran-Pakistan Border Region By Daud Khattak October 20, 2026 14:04 CET The Landscape Of Militancy In The Iran-Pakistan Border Region Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google People and police officers gather after a blast near a railway track in Quetta, the regional capital of Baluchistan in Pakistan, on May 24. Increasing militant attacks along Iran's border with Pakistan over the past few months by multiple armed groups have stoked fears of further instability in the two countries, both of which are already facing multifaceted threats of sectarian violence in addition to the broader repercussions of the conflict in the Middle East. Widespread poverty, underdevelopment, and religious discrimination are believed to be the main drivers of violence in the roughly 900-kilometer porous border region inhabited on both sides by mostly ethnic Baluch. In Pakistan's restive Balochistan Province, Baluch separatists have ramped up their campaign of sophisticated attacks -- including the hijacking of a passenger train in 2025 and the deployment of suicide bombers, including women -- and in Iran's southeastern Sistan-Baluchistan Province a simmering insurgency has intensified since the start of the US war with Iran in February. Unlike the Iranian Baluch, whose armed struggle is rooted in ethnic and religious discrimination, the insurgency in Pakistan's Balochistan is largely secular and revolves around demands for control over the region's rich natural resources. SEE ALSO: Iran's Security Challenges Compounded By Rising Domestic Insurgency The area is also home to two strategic ports: Gwadar on the Pakistani side and Chahbahar in Iran's Sistan-Baluchistan. Analysts say that militant groups have benefited from the complex nature of Iran-Pakistan relations shaped by sectarian and religious differences, competing foreign policy priorities, and divergent geostrategic interests. In January 2024, Iran carried out missile and drone strikes inside Pakistan, targeting the anti-regime militant group Jaish al-Adl. Pakistan retaliated with air strikes, saying Iran was sheltering the separatist Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA) and the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). Iran-Based Militant Groups The Hong Kong-based Silk Road Economic Development Center (SREDC) documented at least 11 attacks during September in Iran's Sistan-Baluchistan targeting Iranian security personnel. Five more attacks were recorded between October 1 and 8 -- all of which were claimed by the Popular Resistance Front, an anti-regime coalition of Baluch organizations that joined forces in late 2025 comprising Jaish al-Nasr, the Pada Baloch Movement, the Mohammad Rasul Allah Group, and Jaish al-Adl. Jaish al-Adl, or the Army of Justice, is one of the deadliest militant groups based in Iran. It was formed in 2012 following the execution of Abdolmalek Rigi, an ethnic Iranian Baluch who led the Sunni Salafi jihadist organization Jundullah. Both Jandullah and Jaish al-Adl claimed to fight for the religious rights of Iranians in Sistan-Baluchestan Province. Because neither group explicitly sought an independent Baluchistan, however, separatists in Pakistan's Balochistan Province view Jaish al-Adl as a proxy of the Pakistani state. Jaish al-Adl is designated as a terrorist group by Iran and the United States. SEE ALSO: Separatist Group Jaish Al-Adl Rebrands As Wider Iranian Opposition The group is known for its guerilla tactics, including ambushes and the use of remote-controlled explosives targeting the officers and members of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC), government figures, as well as Sunni leaders who support the regime. "Jaish al-Adl is adopting more complex attack patterns resembling those of the BLA and fighters from both groups have used the border region for sanctuary or logistics," said Islamabad-based analyst Iftikhar Firdous. Pakistan-Based Militant Groups While religious extremists such as the Islamic State Khorasan Province (ISKP) and the Tehrik-e Taliban Pakistan (TTP) operate in Pakistan's Balochistan Province and account for a number of the 131 attacks recorded in Baluchistan in September, according to the Pakistan Institute for Security Studies, Baluch separatists have gained significant strength in the region over the past few years. The two factions of the Baluchistan Liberation Army (BLA) -- BLA Jeeyand and BLA Azad -- have expanded their operations from local hit-and-runs to setting their sights on high-value targets in cities as far away as Karachi. The BLF is the second most-active group that focuses on guerilla ambushes, attacks on infrastructure, and operating specialized units for more sophisticated attacks. Other smaller separatist groups include the Baluchistan Liberation Guard, the Baluch Republican Army, and the Baluch Nationalist Army. SEE ALSO: Attacks On Chinese Projects Test China-Pakistan 'Iron Brotherhood' In Balochistan Of those, the BLA and BLF are widely involved in attacks on the Pakistani security forces, as well as targeting Chinese-led projects and workers in the region. In 2015, China launched the multibillion-dollar China-Pakistan Economic Corridor Project (CPEC), a key component of Beijing's Belt and Road Initiative that includes rail, road, and infrastructure investment across Pakistan -- with a particular focus on the development of the Gwadar Port and the excavation of mineral resources such as gold, copper and coal in Baluchistan. In November 2018, several separatist groups formed Baluch Raaji Aajoi Sangar to coordinate their attacks against the Pakistani state, which they accused of plundering the region's resources. Since then, the Baluch separatists have not only intensified attacks on Pakistani security agencies but also targeted Chinese nationals in Baluchistan and the neighboring province of Sindh. Cross-Border Connections The Baluch militant groups on either side of the border between Iran and Pakistan have little in common ideologically. "Unlike the Iranian Baluch groups, whose leadership is coming from religious seminaries and hard-liner Sunni Muslims, the leadership of the Baluch groups in Pakistan's Baluchistan Province is mostly university graduates and secular-minded," said Norway-based researcher Kiyya Baloch. "There are no linkages regarding their agendas. Rather, often they accuse each other of being used as proxies by Iran and Pakistan because groups such as Jaish al-Adl have their hiding places on the Pakistani side, while some Baluch groups are said to have their sanctuaries on the Iranian side," he told RFE/RL. Abdul Sayed, a Sweden-based researcher of jihadi movements, said the Iranian and Pakistani Baluch groups may have camps or bases in proximity to one another, but they oppose different states. "Each side accuses the other of acting as a proxy for its respective opponent," he told RFERL, adding that some of these groups have accused one another of killing their members, as has occurred on several occasions between the BLF and Jaish al-Adl. SEE ALSO: What's Behind The Unprecedented Attacks In Pakistan’s Balochistan? Pakistan and Iran have a history of suspicion regarding border management. The most visible demonstration of those differences was seen when Iran and Pakistan each carried out attacks against targets in the other country in January 2024. Iran has long accused Pakistan of supporting militants who oppose the regime in Tehran. Following a suicide attack in Iran's Sistan-Baluchistan that killed 42 people in 2009, a senior Iranian official had asked Islamabad to hand over Jundullah leader Regi. In March 2016, Pakistan announced the arrest of an alleged Indian spy, Kulbhushan Jadhav, from Mashkel area near the Iranian border. https://www.rferl.org/a/stephen-hubbard-.body: News US Citizen Accused By Moscow Of Fighting For Ukraine Released From Russian Prison By RFE/RL October 21, 2026 11:53 CET Updated October 21, 2026 12:57 CET US Citizen Accused By Moscow Of Fighting For Ukraine Released From Russian Prison Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google In this screen shot from handout footage taken and released by the Moscow City Court press service, US citizen Stephen Hubbard attends his verdict hearing in the Russian capital on October 7, 2024. Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired US schoolteacher from Michigan who was accused of joining the Ukrainian armed forces and had been held by Russia since the beginning of Moscow's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, has been freed in what is being framed as a goodwill gesture from the Kremlin. Russian President Vladimir Putin announced Hubbard's release on October 21 as be began his latest round of talks -- their ninth meeting -- with US envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg, which focused on negotiating an end to the war in Ukraine. Putin said Hubbard, the only US prisoner held by Russia with the designation by Washington as "wrongfully detained," was at St. Petersburg's Pulkovo Airport, where he will fly back to the United States with Witkoff. SEE ALSO: US Envoy Witkoff Begins Meeting With Putin After Zelenskyy Talks On Ukraine Peace Shortly afterward, US President Donald Trump confirmed Hubbard's release, saying he would soon be reunited with his family. "Welcome home, Stephen. It's great to have you back," he wrote on Truth Social. Trump said he had "requested" Hubbard's release during a phone call with Putin last week and that Washington "was not required to give anything in return," describing the Kremlin's move as "unprecedented." Following the latest call between the US and Russian presidents, Trump announced a deal to encourage Russian diesel exports and waived sanctions that were due to be imposed under a law he signed last month. Kyiv and its Western allies had warned that these developments could further fuel Moscow's war machine. Hubbard was detained by Russian forces in April 2022. He was later sentenced by the Moscow City Court in October 2024 to six years and 10 months in prison on charges of being a mercenary. Russian prosecutors claimed that he had fought for Ukraine's territorial defense forces in the northeastern Kharkiv region, which was then heavily occupied by Russian forces, under a contract worth $1,000 per month. Hubbard's family, particularly his sister Patricia Fox, had previously expressed doubts about the accusations, stating that Hubbard had long been sympathetic to Russia and had moved to Ukraine in 2014. Fox revealed that Hubbard had lived in the city of Izyum after splitting up with his Ukrainian girlfriend and was there when the war broke out. She also pointed to a video released in May 2022, in which Hubbard was seen commenting on the war. In the video, he claimed to have witnessed Ukrainian forces shelling Izyum for "propaganda purposes," and expressed understanding for Putin's decision to invade Ukraine. It remains unclear under what circumstances the video was made, raising questions about whether Hubbard was coerced into making the statements. There were no reports or official statements about his arrest or how he ended up in Moscow. SEE ALSO: 'They Remain In Torturous Conditions': The Prisoners Left Behind In Russia After Historic Exchange The subject of US citizens being held in Russian prisons has become a prominent political issue in recent years, with many viewing their cases as part of a broader pattern of Americans being used as leverage in wider geopolitical disputes. Hubbard's release came ahead of November's US midterm elections, which will determine control of Congress, and amid protracted negotiations between Moscow and Kyiv to end Russia's full-scale invasion. The two sides remain far apart on the terms of a potential settlement, with the Kremlin offering no concessions and sticking to its hard-line demands. Under Trump, as well as his predecessor, Joe Biden, Moscow and Washington conducted several major swaps of prisoners held in US and Russian prisons. But Moscow still holds several US citizens, whose cases have yet to be resolved. According to Eric Lebson, chief strategy officer at Global Reach, an advocacy group, who spoke with RFE/RL earlier this year, at least five Americans remain in Russian detention. Other reports put the number as high as 10. https://www.rferl.org/a/georgia-faces-ne.body: Georgia Georgia Faces New Test As Court Weighs Ban On 5 Opposition Parties By Sandro Jupalakiani and Farangis Najibullah October 20, 2026 17:19 CET Georgia Faces New Test As Court Weighs Ban On 5 Opposition Parties Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Leaders of Georgia's Opposition Alliance, speaking at a briefing on October 15, urged supporters to join a protest campaign against the ban. Listen to this article 7 min This audio is automated Learn more BATUMI, Georgia -- Georgia's Constitutional Court will begin hearings on October 21 that seek an outright ban on the country's largest opposition parties, a move critics say would undermine fundamental democratic freedoms in the Caucasus nation. The court will convene for three days in the Black Sea city of Batumi to consider the case brought by the ruling Georgian Dream party, which has been in power since 2012. A final ruling must be delivered by June 24, 2027. Rights groups, the European Union, and others have criticized the ban, saying it could further fracture Georgian politics and society and hinder the country's ties with the West. An alliance of opposition parties in Georgia has vowed to protest the ban "fearlessly and forcefully" with a monthlong series of major rallies across the country. The opposition has denounced the proceedings, describing them as politically motivated and arguing the ruling party is seeking to eliminate its main competitors. Georgian Dream officials, including the party's founder Bidzina Ivanishvili -- a billionaire businessman who amassed a fortune in Russia before serving as Georgia's prime minister from 2012 to 2013 -- have repeatedly threatened to ban the opposition parties, saying the move protects the constitutional order. "We will initiate a legal process that will result in the banning of the [opposition] United National Movement, as well as all its satellite and successor parties," Ivanishvili said ahead of parliamentary elections in 2024. SEE ALSO: With Georgia Sliding Toward Russia, Former President Appeals For Renewed US Attention Georgian Dream has said it needed a constitutional majority in parliament to ban opposition parties. After failing to secure such a majority in the October 2024 elections, the ruling party turned to the Constitutional Court, with Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze stating these parties are "inherently unconstitutional." The lawsuit initially targeted three opposition groups and was subsequently expanded to include five: the United National Movement (UNM), Coalition for Change, Strong Georgia – Lelo, the Federalists, and For Georgia. The four opposition groups that crossed the electoral threshold in the 2024 elections received nearly 800,000 votes -- more than a third of all ballots -- combined, according to Georgia's Central Election Commission. The Federalists, established shortly before the elections, have not yet contested a parliamentary election. All five parties support closer ties with the West and Georgia's integration with the European Union and NATO. Nika Gvaramia, a leader of the Coalition for Change, said the aim of the ban was not about depriving opposition politicians of their positions but "about depriving the country of democracy." Some opposition groups said they would kick off a series of rallies starting at Tbilisi State University on October 25. They said the protest campaign, called "Georgia Without Ivanishvili," would run through November 28 -- the second anniversary of widespread protests following Georgian Dream's move to halt EU integration. Allegations Of Unconstitutional Activity The plaintiffs in the case argue that the five parties share unconstitutional goals, including seeking to overthrow or violently change Georgia's constitutional order, undermining the country's independence, and violating its territorial integrity. The case also accuses the opposition parties of seeking to escalate tensions with Russia and bring Georgia into confrontation with Moscow. Much of the supporting material comes from the findings of a temporary parliamentary investigative commission led by Georgian Dream lawmaker Tea Tsulukiani. SEE ALSO: Georgia's Iran Embrace Is Costing It Washington The commission examined the period when the UNM was in power, including the August 2008 war with Russia, as well as subsequent political developments. Founded by former President Mikheil Saakashvili, the party governed Georgia from 2003 to 2012. Opposition parties and rights groups have challenged the legal basis of the proceedings and questioned the commission's impartiality. Transparency International called the commission "an illegal mechanism created by Georgian Dream to destroy opposition parties and eliminate pluralistic democracy in the country." The ruling party has defended its initiative as an effort to protect Georgia's constitutional order. It has also indicated that more parties could face similar proceedings in the future, depending on their political influence. Tinatin Khidasheli, a former defense minister who chairs the Georgian civil society think tank Civic IDEA, said the scale of the proposed bans raised fundamental questions about Georgia's democratic system. "Once a country starts banning political parties on such a scale, it becomes difficult to speak of any compatibility with a democratic system," Khidasheli told RFE/RL. The case comes amid worsening relations between Georgia and its Western partners and a growing crackdown on dissent. Protesters in Tbilisi wave flags during a pro-Europe rally ahead of the 2024 parliamentary elections. Georgia received European Union candidate status in 2023, but its accession process has effectively stalled. In November 2024, Georgian Dream announced it would not seek to open membership talks before the end of 2028, triggering large-scale pro-European demonstrations. The authorities' response to the protests has drawn criticism from human rights groups, which have reported arbitrary arrests, police violence, and pressure on independent media and civil society. George Melashvili, a Georgian political scientist and civic activist, said the case was aimed at consolidating the ruling party's power. "Its sole and primary objective is to establish total control and deprive society of the right to choose," he told RFE/RL. The case also raises questions about Georgia's foreign policy direction and Russia's potential gains from the country's growing isolation from the West. Moscow has long opposed Georgia's efforts to integrate with Western institutions. Melashvili argued that outlawing pro-Western opposition groups would serve Russian interests by weakening those forces and reducing the prospects for Western engagement. https://www.rferl.org/a/us-china-critica.body: China US Grapples With China-Linked Critical Minerals Shortfall Left Unresolved By Trump-Xi Summit By Matthew Fulco October 21, 2026 07:27 CET US Grapples With China-Linked Critical Minerals Shortfall Left Unresolved By Trump-Xi Summit Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google A worker drives a skip loader while working at the site of a rare earth metals mine in China. (file photo) WASHINGTON -- When US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping met in Washington last month, they failed to make headway on one of the most contentious issues in the bilateral relationship: Beijing’s sweeping critical minerals export restrictions that have roiled Pentagon and commercial supply chains alike. Trump and Xi agreed to extend a trade truce -- set to expire on November 10 -- by two months. But the extension doesn’t address Washington’s core concerns about inadequate minerals exports from China. During testimony in July before the Senate Finance Committee, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said that China’s mineral exports are “not as much as we would want. It’s not at the pace we would want.” SEE ALSO: Trump, Xi Strike Stabilizing Tone At Beijing Summit Shaped By Iran Conflict China dominates global production and refining of critical minerals and rare earth permanent magnets, which retain their magnetic properties indefinitely without the need for external power. Rare earth permanent magnets are essential for the functionality of everything from electrical vehicle motors and wind turbines to fighter jets and missile guidance systems. The International Energy Agency (IEA), an autonomous intergovernmental organization based in Paris, estimates that China is the top refiner for 19 out of 20 key strategic minerals, with an average market share of 70 percent. China has an even tighter grip on permanent magnets with a 94 percent global market share, according to the IEA. Beijing has weaponized its critical minerals dominance to counter US sanctions on its semiconductor sector and the Trump administration’s tariffs. It has calibrated the export controls to inflict maximum pressure on Pentagon supply chains while avoiding large-scale disruption to consumer industries, which would risk escalation with Washington that China’s ruling Communist Party (CCP) does not want. Overall, China exported 512 metric tons of rare-earth permanent magnets to the US in August, down 21 percent from July and 13 percent from a year earlier, according to Chinese customs data. Heading into the summit, Xi sought to leverage China’s strategic metals dominance to secure a lasting trade truce with the United States, says Tomasz Nadrowski, portfolio manager at the New York-based Amvest Terraden Critical Minerals Fund. “China has this spigot that it can turn on and off -- which determines the flow of critical minerals to the US and other countries,” he told RFE/RL in an interview. “Extending the trade truce two years would have given this tool additional value,” further locking in US dependency on China’s critical mineral supply chains. The Trump administration was concerned that with a two-year truce, “everyone [both commercial and defense manufacturers] would relax and think, 'We don’t need to build any new capacity,” he says. SEE ALSO: China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy “The US cannot afford to accept strategic chokepoint dependencies for inputs that are essential to our defense industrial base and foundational industries like automotive,” Mahnaz Khan, vice president of policy for critical supply chains at the Silverado Policy Accelerator in Washington, said in an interview. The two-month truce agreed to by Trump and Xi “buys the United States time, but it doesn’t eliminate the underlying vulnerability,” she said Partnering With Central Asia As it works to reduce critical minerals dependence on China, the Trump administration has cast a wide net. In an August fact sheet , the White House said it has signed or approved more than 160 mineral deals since January 2025, totaling about $40 billion. While the administration prioritizes domestic minerals production, in some cases, overseas projects are more feasible. This holds true for tungsten, which the United States has not produced at home since 2015. Tungsten is a crucial input for military-grade steel, aerospace components, munitions, and ground vehicle armor. Given its high density, the metal is used for stabilization and control in missiles and aircraft. Tungsten’s importance for defense led the Trump administration to throw its support behind a $1.1 billion project in Kazakhstan. Under an agreement signed in November 2025 between US-based Cove Capital (now known as the Cove Kaz Capital Group) and the state-run Kazakh mining company Tau-Ken Samruk, the two parties will jointly develop one of the world’s largest tungsten resources. “Kazakhstan made a conscious political choice to make an award to a US company, though rumor has it that China was also bidding for the same project,” Akbota Karibayeva Meyer, a research fellow at the Caspian Policy Center in Washington, told RFE/RL. The decision exemplifies Kazakhstan’s multi-vector foreign policy, which aims to preserve strategic autonomy by balancing ties with major powers, she explains. SEE ALSO: US Revisits Georgia's Black Sea Port As Strategic Corridors Rise Drilling, feasibility studies, and site preparation began after the agreement’s formal closing. Yet full commercial production is several years away. “Are these projects in Kazakhstan viable? Sure, they’re viable. The economics are very hard to pencil out without a subsidy, though,” Ian Lange, a professor at the Colorado School of Mines and deputy director of its Critical Materials Innovation Hub, said in an interview. “Ideally, I might want to do something [in terms of a mining investment] that limits the government’s expenditure and provides for some competition,” he says. The Trump administration is also working with Uzbekistan to source critical minerals. In February, the US commodities firm Traxys signed a $1 billion deal with the Uzbek government focused on the exploration and extraction of tungsten, molybdenum, and copper. This agreement aligns with a separate critical minerals pact reached between the US International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and Uzbekistan. Elsewhere in Central Asia, the potential for cooperation with the US exists. Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan both have major reserves of antimony, a critical mineral used as a flame retardant, an alloying agent for lead, and a compound in semiconductors. During a September visit to Bishkek, US Special Envoy for South and Central Asia Sergio Gor and US Senator Steve Daines, chairman of the Senate Central Asia Caucus, discussed mining cooperation with Kyrgyz officials. SEE ALSO: China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy During their trip, they also met with the presidents of Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Tajikstan. While the US continues to make progress sourcing critical minerals from Central Asia, “it is important to recognize the limiting factor of geography,” Karibayeva Meyer says. Given its proximity to Central Asia, “it is much easier for China to be involved in the region.” Short And Long-Term Challenges In the short term, the US faces a key hurdle in its critical minerals diversification push: from January 1, 2027, the Pentagon will prohibit the use of certain metals sourced from the “foreign adversary countries” of China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran. The ban, outlined in Executive Order 14415 , sharply narrows the possibility of receiving waivers for the use of rare-earth magnets, tungsten, tantalum, and molybdenum from those four nations. https://www.rferl.org/a/us-russia-talks-.body: News US Envoy Witkoff Begins Meeting With Putin After Zelenskyy Talks On Ukraine Peace By RFE/RL October 21, 2026 09:43 CET Updated October 21, 2026 11:29 CET US Envoy Witkoff Begins Meeting With Putin After Zelenskyy Talks On Ukraine Peace Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google US President Donald Trump's special envoy, Steve Witkoff (left), is greeted by Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev upon his arrival in Saint Petersburg on October 21. US envoy Steve Witkoff has begun his meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Constantine Palace in St. Petersburg, according to news reports, a day after holding talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Oslo. The meeting in St. Petersburg is the ninth to take place between Witkoff and the Russian leader. Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov said that Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, would not personally attend proceedings due to illness, and reportedly will join the meeting virtually. "We have some clear ideas on how to get to peace," Zelenskyy told reporters after the talks, which were hosted by Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store and Finnish President Alexander Stubb in Oslo on October 20. "We want the Americans to take these ideas to the Russians," Zelenskyy said, adding that "one of the important ideas is to move to a potential trilateral meeting of the leaders to address the issues that only the leaders can do." Trump commented on the possibility of direct talks between Putin and Zelenskyy, saying the two leaders did not need to meet face-to-face to reach a deal. "They don't have to be in the same room. I guess they can do it another way," Trump told reporters on October 20. Missile Intelligence 'Works Now,' Says Zelenskyy US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is visiting India, described Witkoff's talks with Zelenskyy in Oslo as "positive." "It was positive, nothing unexpected, nothing surprising, and he'll now, armed with those ideas, be able to go to St. Petersburg and share them with the Russian side -- and let's see if we can make some progress," Rubio told reporters on October 21. Zelenskyy said he was grateful to the US for providing intelligence on Russian missile strikes, adding that early-warning systems were now working effectively. "We are thankful that intelligence works.... I'm speaking about early warning, which is very important for our people, for children, adults, civilians, because we can hear when ballistic [missiles are] coming," Zelenskyy told reporters in the Norwegian capital. Embed share Funeral Held For Five Children From One Ukrainian Family Killed In Russian Strike In July by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:01:29 0:00 Zelenskyy reiterated that Kyiv had immediately backed the American proposal for an energy cease-fire, but Russia continued its attacks, highlighting the need for strong security guarantees for Ukraine. Meanwhile, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was seeking a lasting peace rather than a cease-fire, in response to Kyiv's call for an energy truce. Stubb said the Oslo talks had yielded "genuine progress" on both the long-term outlook and more immediate issues. He said the participants had identified "some elements of peace" in the broader picture, along with key points concerning security and the economy. Russian Attacks Continue Amid Talks Amid ongoing talks, Moscow continued its attacks on Ukraine, killing at least four people as Russian drone and missile strikes hit several regions overnight. A Russian air strike on Kyiv on October 21 killed two people and injured two others, damaging a 24-story residential building, Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported . Emergency power outages were reported in several parts of the Ukrainian capital following Russian attacks, as energy workers worked to restore electricity, the energy company DTEK reported on October 21. Russian Drone Hits Kyiv Apartment Building, Killing Two by RFE/RL No media source currently available 0:00 0:00:34 0:00 In the Kharkiv region, a Russian drone attack killed an 81-year-old woman and an 83-year-old man, according to regional authorities. In the Lviv region, local authorities said Russian drone "attacked an enterprise" overnight, injuring two workers and damaging a nearby private house with falling debris. Russia attacked Ukraine overnight with cruise missiles and 186 attack drones, Ukraine's Air Force reported on October 21. Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces had launched drone strikes against Ukraine’s logistics hubs, port infrastructure, and vessels. It also reported that Russian air defenses had intercepted and destroyed 373 Ukrainian drones across multiple Russian regions. Imprisoned American Released At the Putin-Witkoff meeting, which was being broadcast on a video feed, both men confirmed the release of Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old native of Michigan who was captured by Russian troops in April 2022 and accused of being a mercenary for Ukrainian forces. Putin said Hubbard was at St. Petersburg's Pulkovo Airport, where he will fly back to the United States with Witkoff. Trump had said on October 20 ahead of Witkoff's visit that he had asked Putin to release Hubbard. "I've been talking to him at length. I've asked him to release him. Let's see what happens," Trump told journalists in Washington. In 2024, a Russian court sentenced Hubbard to seven years in prison. https://www.rferl.org/a/rubio-central-as.body: News Analysis Rubio Trip Highlights US Push For Deeper Ties With Central Asia By Alex Raufoglu October 20, 2026 12:54 CET Rubio Trip Highlights US Push For Deeper Ties With Central Asia Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (right) waves next to his wife, Jeanette Dousdebes Rubio, as they board a plane to leave Samarkand on October 20. SAMARKAND, Uzbekistan -- US Secretary of State Marco Rubio departed Uzbekistan on October 20 for India after meetings with all five Central Asian countries, wrapping up a visit aimed at expanding Washington’s economic and diplomatic engagement with a region increasingly intent on shaping its own international partnerships. Rubio’s visit to the historic Silk Road city of Samarkand brought together the foreign ministers of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan. He also met Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoev and attended a US-Uzbekistan business council event alongside a delegation of nearly 300 American business leaders. The visit produced several concrete initiatives, including Uzbekistan’s signing of the US-led Artemis Accords on peaceful space exploration and a bilateral investment agreement that the parties said would total $12 billion when implemented. Ambassador To Uzbekistan Says Washington Supports 'Sovereignty' For Central Asia by RFE/RL No media source currently available 0:00 0:01:04 0:00 But the broader significance of Rubio’s trip may lie less in the immediate announcements than in Washington’s renewed attention to Central Asia -- and its stated willingness to pursue closer ties without demanding that regional governments choose between the US, Russia, and China. “This is not simply a contest between outside powers,” US Ambassador to Uzbekistan Jonathan Henick told RFE/RL in an interview as Rubio departed Samarkand. Henick said Central Asian countries had demonstrated their independence and their ability to determine the terms of their own international relationships over the 35 years since the collapse of the Soviet Union. The United States, he said, wants to offer them additional options, both politically and economically, that would help them preserve their independence and expand their room for maneuver. A Renewed Place On Washington’s Strategic Map Henick said Rubio’s visit represented a historic expansion of American engagement, with growing economic and commercial ties accompanying closer political contacts. But he also stressed that American interests were coinciding with changes already underway in Central Asia, rather than creating them from scratch. SEE ALSO: 'We're Never Going To Be The Major Player': Former Diplomat's Reality Check On US Ambitions In Central Asia Uzbekistan, he said, was in the midst of a historic period of economic reform under Mirziyoev, whose government has sought to create a more business-friendly environment and attract foreign investment. “The coincidence of the attention from Washington with the opportunities that we’re seeing here,” Henick said, was helping drive the transformation. Luke Coffey, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute, offered a more measured assessment of the immediate diplomatic results. Speaking to RFE/RL, Coffey described Rubio’s visit as largely a maintenance exercise intended to keep agreements reached during last year’s White House summit on track. He considered that earlier gathering more consequential than the Samarkand meetings themselves. SEE ALSO: Trump And Central Asia Reach Critical Minerals Deal At Washington Summit Nevertheless, he said, the Trump administration’s broader actions during its second term had collectively returned Central Asia to Washington’s strategic map -- a development he welcomed. All five Central Asian states retain significant commercial and diplomatic links with Russia, while China remains a major regional economic power. Their relationships with Iran also vary. Rubio acknowledged that reality during his visit, saying countries wanted as many international relationships as possible. Uzbekistan, he noted, had made clear that it wanted to be friends with everybody. No Demand To Choose Between Washington, Moscow, Beijing The question of whether Washington can expand its influence without pressuring Central Asian governments to distance themselves from Russia and China emerged as a central theme of the visit. Henick rejected the notion that the region should be viewed primarily through the lens of competition among outside powers. “For too long we’ve been characterizing this region as, you know, as sometimes they call it the Great Game,” he said. “It’s outside powers competing in the region. Honestly, I think that completely mischaracterizes what’s happening here.” Coffey agreed that the US should not seek to force regional governments to choose Washington over Moscow or Beijing. SEE ALSO: China Looks To Shore Up Influence In Central Asia After US Minerals Diplomacy Geography, economic ties, history, and cultural connections make such a choice unrealistic, he said. Instead, Washington should remain actively engaged and help its partners balance their relationships with major powers. Angela Howard, a research analyst at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies’ Center on Economic and Financial Power, said Rubio’s approach could make it easier for Washington to establish partnerships that might otherwise be blocked by an insistence on choosing sides. The administration is signaling that it is interested in the region, prepared to compete with Russia and China, and prioritizing economic statecraft, Howard said. An approach that avoids an “us-versus-them” framework could allow the United States to provide alternatives to Russia, China, and Iran incrementally, she added. Howard argued that Washington would make more progress in limiting its competitors’ influence by pursuing specific policy changes -- including action against sanctions-evasion networks -- than by issuing ultimatums that Central Asian governments would be unlikely to accept. Investment Remains The Real Test The visit’s economic agenda was underscored by the large business delegation accompanying Rubio, as the administration seeks greater access to Central Asia’s markets and natural resources, including critical minerals. During his visit, Rubio defended the commercial dimension of American diplomacy, saying the United States wanted fair competition and an opportunity for its companies. At a business council event, he also argued that US foreign policy should not focus so heavily on immediate crises that it neglects long-term opportunities. “Our focus on a problem region or a problem country or a problem issue in the world still has to be there, but it cannot come at the expense of embracing opportunities,” Rubio said. “You have to be able to do both.” Henick said the visit had helped businesses already working on deals make progress in their relationships and introduced other American companies to opportunities in Uzbekistan for the first time. He expected many of those first-time visitors to return. Uzbekistan’s signature on the Artemis Accords could also open new avenues for cooperation in space exploration, the ambassador said. SEE ALSO: Kazakh Plan To Join Chinese-Led Moon Base Would Strengthen Space Partnership Washington and Tashkent are continuing to work on other projects that Henick hopes will be ready in time for Mirziyoev’s planned trip to the United States to attend the G20 summit in Florida as an official observer. Another issue on the bilateral agenda is the Jackson-Vanik amendment, a Cold War-era US trade provision that continues to apply to Uzbekistan and several other countries. Henick said the provisions were routinely waived and did not significantly affect the embassy’s day-to-day work, but acknowledged their symbolic importance to the countries still covered by the measure. Levine was assaulted by masked settlers despite wearing a clearly marked “Press” vest. CPJ’s October 17 letter emphasized the Israeli government’s “obligation to swiftly, thoroughly, and impartially investigate all attacks against journalists, including identifying perpetrators and holding them fully accountable under criminal law.” Such investigations should examine the actions of Israeli military or police personnel, including any failure to intervene or to protect journalists, CPJ said. On October 17, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee posted on X that the U.S. had called for “a full investigation, arrest, and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law to whoever participated.” Multiple members of Congress also strongly condemned the assault, calling on Israel to hold the perpetrators to account and end the culture of impunity for attacks on journalists. CPJ’s letter highlighted that Levine’s brutal assault fits a broader pattern of violence against journalists in the West Bank and called on the Israeli government to commit to a clear timeline for investigations, including public updates on their progress, and to cease downplaying such assaults as that contributes to an enabling environment for future attacks against journalists. https://cpj.org/2026/10/cpj-condemns-dig.body: Share this: Share on Bluesky (Opens in new window) Bluesky Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on WhatsApp (Opens in new window) WhatsApp Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email Miami, October 19, 2026—The Committee to Protect Journalists condemns the digital harassment and doxxing of exiled Iranian investigative journalist and cybersecurity expert Mohammad Jorjandi and his family. Living in the U.S. since 2016, Jorjandi is the founder of Webamooz, an independent outlet covering cybercrime and online financial fraud for Persian-speaking audiences, with selected investigations in English . His investigations have exposed alleged links between Iranian state-connected entities and illegal payment processing for gambling networks, VPN sales, consumer fraud involving the state telecommunications network and affiliated companies, and cryptocurrency embezzlement. Jorjandi said actors linked to fraud networks he has exposed are behind the attacks and have repeatedly used Iran’s judiciary to target him, alongside direct state pressure. “Mohammad Jorjandi and his family should not face threats and harassment because of his reporting,” said José Zamora, CPJ’s regional director for the Americas. “Iranian authorities must end their persecution of Jorjandi, and social media platforms must act against threats and the publication of his family’s private information.” He also investigated an alleged fake-degree operation involving NIUTM that he reported was used to defraud Canada’s immigration system and sell fraudulent U.S. university degrees in Iran. A plaintiff who sued him for defamation in Virginia over that reporting withdrew the case on the eve of trial, after nearly two years of litigation. Jorjandi’s subsequent lawsuit against the plaintiff remains pending. Jorjandi says the withdrawal of the lawsuit was followed by a coordinated harassment campaign against him and his family on Telegram and Instagram. Attacks across multiple channels, verified accounts, paid articles, and a website bearing his name have accused him of being an intelligence operative, money launderer, and sanctions evader. They have also published photographs of his relatives, including his elderly father. Inside Iran, subjects of Jorjandi’s reporting have brought multiple criminal cases against him. Judicial authorities have blocked websites carrying his investigations, ordered his channel removed from Iranian platforms, barred Iranian media from mentioning him, and characterized his journalism as sedition and incitement. He has also received a two-year prison sentence in absentia and faces a nationwide arrest warrant. Separately, Jorjandi told CPJ that individuals based in Germany, presenting themselves as opponents of Iran’s government, have targeted him since late 2025. In near-daily Clubhouse and Telegram sessions, they have disclosed his family’s address in Iran, published a photograph of his elderly father’s front door, and offered money to anyone willing to act against his father. Criminal and civil proceedings Jorjandi initiated in Germany remain pending. Jorjandi said he has repeatedly reported the Telegram channel to no results. CPJ is investigating these attacks and calls on social media platforms to protect Jorjandi and his family from further harassment. https://cpj.org/2026/10/broadcast-journa.body: Share this: Share on Bluesky (Opens in new window) Bluesky Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on WhatsApp (Opens in new window) WhatsApp Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email Bangkok, October 16, 2026 —Philippine authorities must conduct a swift and thorough investigation into the killing of broadcast journalist Adrian “Golden Boy” Loterte, identify and arrest those responsible, and ensure they are brought to justice, the Committee to Protect Journalists said today. Loterte, an anchor at the local “Rabas Cun Rabas” online program on RBN News Television and a freelance broadcaster on DWIZ FM, was shot at about 4:10 p.m. on Monday at his bakery in Barangay San Roque, Daraga, a municipality in the Bicol region’s Albay province, according to a police report . “Authorities must promptly identify, apprehend, and prosecute the perpetrators behind the killing of broadcast journalist Adrian Loterte,” said Shawn Crispin, CPJ’s senior Southeast Asia representative. “Until President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s administration does more to end impunity in media murder cases, these grotesque attacks on the press will continue.” One of two unidentified suspects opened fire before both escaped on a black-and-white Honda Click motorcycle, according to Bicol police spokesperson Lt. Col. Maria Luisa Calubaquib. Police recovered eight spent shells from a .45-caliber pistol at the crime scene. Loterte sustained four gunshot wounds and was pronounced dead on arrival at Daraga Doctors Hospital. In an October 13 briefing , Police Regional Office 5 Director Randy Glenn Silvio said a special investigation task group was established to identify the suspects and their motive, and that investigators were reviewing CCTV footage to trace the perpetrators’ movements before and after the crime. Silvio said police were examining possible work, personal and business-related motives. The Presidential Task Force on Media Security (PTFOMS), a state body tasked with investigating media murders, said it had also opened an investigation into Loterte’s killing and was coordinating with law enforcement agencies, without speculating on a motive. The Philippine National Police and PTFOMS did not immediately respond to CPJ’s emailed requests for comment. CPJ research shows that the Philippines is consistently among the top nations worldwide where media murders go unresolved. https://cpj.org/2026/10/pakistan-media-r.body: Share this: Share on Bluesky (Opens in new window) Bluesky Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Share on LinkedIn (Opens in new window) LinkedIn Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on WhatsApp (Opens in new window) WhatsApp Email a link to a friend (Opens in new window) Email New York, October 16, 2026—The Committee to Protect Journalists urges Pakistan authorities to withdraw sweeping restrictions preventing television network broadcasts from airing live coverage of terrorist attacks and other vaguely defined “unpleasant” incidents. Journalists and media workers must be able to report breaking news and current affairs independently, free from fear of legal retaliation, and in the public interest. On October 13, the Pakistan Electronic Media Regulatory Authority (PEMRA) ordered all satellite television channels to refrain from broadcasting, rebroadcasting, or airing live coverage of any “unfortunate” or “unpleasant” incident, including explosions, blasts, shootings, and terrorist attacks, according to a copy of the directive reviewed by CPJ. Warning of legal action against broadcasters that don’t comply, PEMRA said they can only air information that has been verified by the relevant government departments or law enforcement agencies. Broadcasters must also use time delays and maintain independent editorial boards, according to the directive. “Preventing journalists from independent reporting of major security incidents and requiring them to rely on information authorized by state and security agencies risks turning legitimate safety safeguards into a system of official information control and censorship,” said Waliullah Rahmani, CPJ’s Afghanistan and Pakistan representative. “Pakistani authorities must rescind these sweeping restrictions and allow newsrooms to make responsible editorial decisions without fear of regulatory retaliation.” The directive reiterates restrictions on television channels first issued in February 2023 by PEMRA, which accused TV channels of broadcasting unverified and speculative information during militant attacks. In August, Pakistan’s Ministry of Information and Broadcasting issued guidelines requiring foreign journalist and their associates in Pakistan, as well as those working with international media, to register with the ministry and obtain a certificate before undertaking reporting assignments outside Islamabad, Lahore, and Karachi. The latest directive comes after heightened political-security instability in Pakistan, including the imposition of emergency rule in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Pakistan’s Ministry of Information and Broadcasting did not respond to CPJ’s email seeking comment. https://www.fidh.org/en/en/region/americ.body: 20/10/2026 Press release Mexico en es YURI CORTEZ / AFP The Chair of the Committee on Enforced Disappearances (CED) presented its annual report to the Third Committee of the United Nations (UN) General Assembly, which is responsible for humanitarian and human rights issues. In presenting the report, the CED reaffirmed its call for the situation in Mexico to be discussed as a matter of urgency by the plenary of the multilateral organisation. New York, 20 October 2026. In the report presented on Tuesday, the CED reiterated its decision, in accordance with Article 34 of the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance, that the situation in Mexico should be addressed by the General Assembly, given the existence of well-founded indications that enforced disappearances have been and continue to be perpetrated in the country as crimes against humanity. It also emphasised the importance of this procedure in mobilising international support for the adoption of preventive measures that will enable Mexico to tackle the crisis effectively. The International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH), IDHEAS Idheas Litigio Estratégico en Derechos Humanos, its member organisation in Mexico, and the undersigned collectives of relatives of disappeared persons would like to express our gratitude for the work carried out by the CED. We fully support its decision, as it acknowledges the existence of international crimes that are emblematic of what victims are experiencing in the country and seeks to contribute to the adoption of measures aimed at preventing, investigating, punishing and eradicating such conducts. The situation of Mexico is already on the agenda of the UN General Assembly. All that remains now is to identify the most appropriate time and the best way to discuss it. We, the undersigned organisations, call on the Member States of the Assembly to devise a mechanism that allows for the broad participation of victims from Mexico and the region in the examination of the country’s grave situation. Furthermore, we urge the Mexican State to approach the implementation of this procedure in a constructive manner. International technical assistance can provide a key opportunity to strengthen the investigation and prosecution of enforced disappearances, particularly in addressing patterns of collusion between public officials and organised crime. The effective investigation of the various forms of collusion, participation, acquiescence or omission on the part of public authorities in the commission of these crimes remains an unresolved issue, which has not only reinforced their structural impunity but has also contributed to their recurrence. With regard to the announcement made by the Federal Public Prosecutor’s Office (Fiscalía General de la República - FGR) concerning its comprehensive reform and internal strengthening, it is essential that this process takes into account the requests that the relatives of disappeared persons have repeatedly made regarding the administration of justice. Firstly, it is imperative that the FGR makes progress in shedding light on enforced disappearances; to this end, it must recognise their systematic nature by identifying the patterns within which they occurred. Secondly, a national debate must be launched on transitional justice mechanisms or those that recognise effective cooperation in criminal proceedings. This would provide the public prosecutor’s offices with the tools to grant conditional criminal leniency in exchange for the provision of truthful and detailed information, thereby enabling progress to be made in identifying those responsible and the structures of corruption that underpin and facilitate enforced disappearances. Violence perpetrated by organised crime is an international scourge, in the face of which we must move forward in building a global alliance in favor of life and against policies of terror, death and war. For this reason, it is urgent that the Mexican State recognise that international cooperation based on respect for human rights standards will strengthen its efforts to prevent and eradicate enforced disappearances, whilst respecting national sovereignty and human security. Furthermore, the State must engage in dialogue with the families of disappeared persons and the organisations supporting them, so as, on the one hand, to address the victims’ demands for truth and justice arising from the security policies implemented in the country. On the other hand, it must complement the National Search Strategy with measures specifically targeted at those areas where cases remain unpunished and the authorities continue to fail to carry out an effective search for disappeared persons. Background: implementation of the procedure under Article 34 and the Mexican State’s response In April 2026, following a request by the FIDH to initiate the procedure under Article 34, the CED concluded that the information submitted by civil society organisations and the State gave it sufficient cause for concern to refer the matter to the General Assembly for consideration. In its decision , the CED noted that, since 2006, enforced disappearances had increased exponentially in the country. According to official records, as of February 2026, the number of disappeared and untraced persons stood at over 130,000. In these cases, impunity was almost absolute. The information analysed by the CED indicated that, since 2006, disappearances had been and continued to be committed as crimes against humanity, as they were directed against the civilian population and occurred on a widespread and systematic basis at different times and in different parts of Mexican territory. This nature was reflected not only in the sheer scale and geographical spread of the cases, but also in the fact that they followed similar criminal patterns, within the framework of planned operations, demonstrating that their recurrence was not accidental. According to the CED, the perpetration of enforced disappearances was in some cases directly attributable to public authorities and in others to criminal organisations, such as drug cartels, which acted both autonomously and in collusion with state officials. It stated that, in many cases, the available information showed that organised crime perpetrated the enforced disappearances " with the complicity and, at a minimum, the acquiescence of public officials at the federal, state and municipal levels ". Following the referral of the situation in Mexico to the UN General Assembly, the CED alerted the plenary to the need to provide technical cooperation, financial support and specialised assistance required by the authorities for the search for disappeared persons and the thorough investigation of these cases. Despite this call for cooperation, the Mexican State reacted negatively to the CED’s invocation of the Article 34 procedure. In an official statement , the Government rejected the decision, describing it as biased, lacking in legal accuracy and based on premises that did not correspond to reality. Moreover, it attacked the members of the international mechanism, pointing to alleged conflicts of interest that compromised the impartiality of their work. БАҚ өкілдеріне ғимаратта депутаттармен тек ұйымдастырылған баспасөз жиынында және тек белгіленген күн тәртібі туралы сөйлесуге рұқсат етіледі деген жаңа талап енгізілді. Парламент қызметкерлері ол талаптар журналистерді аккредиттеу ережелері мен БАҚ туралы заңға сүйеніп қабылданғанын айтқан. Мұндай оқиғалар елде тәуелсіз БАҚ-қа қысым күшейіп, журналистердің Құрылтайда сұрақ қоюы қиындаған тұста болып отыр. Бұған дейін осы ережені орындамаған тілшілердің біріне ескерту берілген еді. Мұндай норманы "Әділ сөз " баспасөз қорғау ұйымы сынап, ішкі ережелер сөз еркіндігі мен ақпарат алу құқығына берілген кепілдіктерді алмастырмауы керек деп мәлімдеген. Журналистерді қорғау комитеті (CPJ) мен сөз бостандығын және адам құқықтарын қорғайтын қазақстандық ұйымдар бұл шектеулерді алып тастауды талап етті. Бұған дейін "Etude-Ybyrai" компаниясы журналист жариялаған материалдар "іскерлік беделге нұқсан келтірді" және "жалған ақпарат таратты" деп сотқа жүгінген. Борейко өзіне тағылған айыптарға нақты айғақ-дәлелдер жоғын айтқан. "Власть" сайтының жазуынша, қорғау жағы экономикалық және филологиялық сараптаманың дұрыс жүргізілгендігіне күмәнданып, нәтижесімен келіспей отыр. Филологиялық сараптаманың нәтижесі Борейко "өзінің материалдарында компания туралы теріс ақпарат таратты" деген тұжырым жасаған. Қорғау жағы мұнымен келіспеді. «Филологиялық сараптамаға келсек, сарапшы талап-арызда көрсетілген талаптардың шегінен шығып кеткен... Ол Вадим Николаевичтің барлық сұрағын біріктіріп, өз бетінше қайта тұжырымдаған. Бұл ретте қай күнгі материал екені, материалдың қайда жарияланғаны, тіпті бұл сөзді кім айтқаны да мүлде нақтыланбаған» деді адвокат Жанна Оразбақова. Қорғау жағы Алматының бұрынғы әкімі Ерболат Досаев, КТК арнасының репортажы, сонымен бірге тұрғындардың видеосы бар бес видеожазбаны біріктіруді сұрады. "Ол жерде Базарбек те, уәкілетті органдардың өкілдері де, мемлекеттік сәулет-құрылыс бақылауы басқарма (ГАСК) өкілдері де пікір білдірген. Сондықтан осы видеоны қарастырғымыз келеді. Өйткені онда Досаевтың Әуезов ауданының тұрғындарымен кездесу кезінде "бұл жерде көпфункциялы тұрғын үй кешені салынбайтыны анық" деп айтқаны бар. Одан кейінгі бейнежазбада ГАСК өкілі құрылыс жұмыстарын жүргізуге берілген рұқсаттың кері қайтарып алынғанын айтады. Әуезов ауданының әкімімен де кездесу болған" деді Оразбақова. "Біреудің айтқанын маған әлі таңып отыр және қателіктер хаттамадан зерттеуге қарай көшіп жатыр" деді Борейко. Қорғау жағы шағым берушінің өзі жауапкердің "жалған ақпарат тарату фактісін" дәлелдеуі керек, бірақ әлі күнге дейін журналисті нақты не үшін айыптап отырғаны түсініксіз деді. Олар сарапшы видеожазбаны мүлде зерттемеді деді. "Сарапшы материалдар мен келтірілген шығын арасындағы себеп-салдарлық қатынасты анықтауға қатысты үш сұрақты мүлде алып тастаған. Ол тек Etude-Ybyrai компаниясының қанша қаражат жұмсағанын факт ретінде көрсетумен шектелген. Алайда бұл шығындардың Борейконың материалдарына ешқандай себеп-салдарлық байланысы жоқ. Компания бетонға, өрт қауіпсіздігіне, техниканы жөндеуге қанша қаражат жұмсағанын көрсеткен. Бірақ мұның бәріне Борейконың әрекеттерінің қатысы жоқ қой" деді Оразбақова. Ал судья Айдар Өтебеков құқықтық баға беруді соттың еншісіне қалдыруды сұраған. Бұған дейін компания 71 млн теңге шығын келгенін айтқан. Экономикалық сараптамадан кейін шығын көлемі 43 млн теңге болды. "Сараптама 43 млн теңге шығын болғанын растады. Бірақ осы шығын мен Вадим Николаевичтің әрекеті арасында себеп-салдарлық қатынас бар ма?" деді қорғау жағының адвокаты Фархад Цай. Филолог-сарапшы сөйлеушілердің кім екенін анықтау өз құзыретіне кірмейтінін айтып, кейбір сұрақтар қайталанғандықтан әрі дұрыс тұжырымдалмағандықтан біріктіріп, түзеткенін түсіндірді. Ал экономист-сарапшылар қаржылық құжаттарды, соның ішінде шарттарды, орындалған жұмыс актілерін, жүкқұжаттар мен төлем мәліметтерін зерттегенін мәлімдеді. Цайдың айтуынша, экономикалық сараптама 71 млн теңгенің тек 43 млн теңгесі шығын ретінде құжатпен расталғанын көрсеткен, алайда оның залал болып саналатынын сот шешеді. Сонымен бірге талапкер жағы филологиялық сараптама қорытындысымен келіспейтінін, өйткені сарапшыға ұсынылған сөз тіркестерінің орнына басқа тіркестерді қарастырғанын мәлімдеді. Келесі сот отырысына дейін 22 қазанда шағым берушілер талаптарын анықтауы керек. Сайттың жазуынша, 20 қазан күні сотта шағым берушінің өкілетіне қатысты сұрақ туындаған. Борейконың ақпаратынша, Etude-Ybyrai компаниясының директоры ауысқан, ал компания атынан сотқа қатысып жатқан Бақыт Қасыбаев сенімхатты жаңартпаған. Осыған байланысты ол сенімхат алу үшін сот залынан шығып кеткен. Келесі сот отырысы 22 қазанда өтеді. "Өткір күректің" жазуынша, сот Вадим Борейконы өз сотынан ақпарат бермеуге міндеттеген. Вадим Борейко Қазақстан билігі туралы сыни хабар шығаратын тәуелсіз журналист ретінде танылған. Биыл ақпанда әлдекімдер оның Facebook пен Instagram-дағы аккаунттарын бұзған. Журналистикада 40 жылдан астам уақыт еңбек етіп жүрген Борейко 2000 жылдары "Время", Forbes.kz , Ratel.kz басылымдарында жұмыс істеп, одан кейін YouTube платформасында "Гиперборей" арнасын ашқан. Жуырда ол арнаның жұмысын белгісіз мерзімге тоқтатты. 2023 жылдың басында белгісіз біреулер Вадим Борейко пәтерінің есігін құрылысқа арналған көбікпен бекітіп кеткен . Ізінше онымен бірге жұмыс істейтін бейнеоператор Роман Егоровтың екі автокөлігін біреулер өртеп кеткен. Егоров бұл әрекеттің кәсіби қызметіне қатысы бар деп санайтынын айтқан. Сол жылы күзде Алматы соты журналистерге шабуыл ұйымдастырды деп айыпталған адамдарға шартты жаза бергені хабарланған (сотталушылардың өзге де журналистерге жасалған шабуылға қатысы бар деп айтылған) . Ин ниҳод рӯзи 21-уми октябр гуфт, Зарина Саймуддинова, сокини 26-солаи ноҳияи Абдураҳмонии Ҷомии вилояти Хатлонро бо гумони дуздии кӯдак боздошт кардааст. Дар сурати исботи иттиҳом ба ин зан аз панҷ то бист сол зиндон таҳдид мекунад. Зарина Саймуддинова Зарина Саймуддинова дар навори бисёр таҳриршудаи мақомот мегӯяд, ки шаш сол боз фарзанд надошт ва барои ҳамин дар фикри дуздидани кӯдак шудааст. Вай дар ин видео, ки маълум нест таҳти чӣ шароит сабт шудааст, гуфт, шаби 11-уми октябр бо либоси тамизкории хушдоманаш, ки дар шаҳри Душанбе кору зиндагӣ мекунад, вориди таваллудхона шуда, навзодро бо худ бурд. "Сипас дар болотари таваллудхона ба таксӣ савор шуда, ба хонаи хушдоманам рафтам. Субҳ ба як таксӣ 250 сомонӣ додем то хонаамон дар ноҳияи Абдураҳмони Ҷомӣ расонд," – афзуд ӯ. Дар навори дурбинҳои назоратӣ, ки Радиои Озодӣ дастрас карда буд, як зани ниқобпӯше дар либоси сабзи тамизкорони таваллудхона кӯдаки навзоде ба даст аз назди зойишгоҳ башитоб дур мешавад. Мақомот дар гузориши худ баъзе аз ҷанбаҳои қазияро норавшан мондаанд. Аз ҷумла, гуфта нашудааст, ки зан махсус барои дуздии кӯдак аз ноҳияи Абдураҳмони Ҷомӣ ба Душанбе омадааст? Чаро маҳз таваллудхонаи рақами яки пойтахтро интихоб кард? Чӣ гуна вориди утоқи зоишгоҳ шуд ва оё касе ӯро надид? Ва хушдомани ӯ кист ва дар куҷо кор мекунад? Зан феълан дар боздоштгоҳ аст. Хабарнигорони Радиои Озодӣ талош доранд, ки пайвандони ӯро пайдо ва асли қазияро аз онҳо бипурсанд. Тифли навзоди Мавзуна Акрамоваи 19-сола ва сокини ноҳияи Нуробод нимашаби 11-уми октябр аз зоишгоҳи Пажӯҳишгоҳи модару кӯдак, муҳимтарин маркази ташхиси тиббӣ ва муолиҷаи модарон ва навзодон дар Тоҷикистон, гум шуд. Ин дар ҳолест, ки вуруд ба ҳуҷраи беморон ё аёдати онҳо дар нимашабӣ дар шифохонаҳои Тоҷикистон мамнуъ аст. Яке аз пайвандони модари тифл ба Радиои Озодӣ гуфт, зане, ки ба кӯдакрабоӣ гумонбар мешавад, ҳамдеҳаи Мавзуна Акрамова аст. Дар Тоҷикистон нопадид шудани навзод аз таваллудхона бисёр кам иттифоқ афтодааст, вале соли 2023 як зани 45-сола аз ноҳияи Хуросонро бо гуноҳи дуздидани тифли дурӯза аз зоишгоҳи ноҳияи Абдураҳмони Ҷомӣ ба 8 сол зиндон маҳкум карданд. Муфаттишон баъд аз як ҳафтаи ҷустуҷӯ тифли навзодро пайдо карданд ва зан ба мақомот гуфтааст, аз тарси онки шавҳараш барои дигар фарзанд наовардан аз ӯ ҷудо мешавад, тифлро дуздид ва ба шавҳари муҳоҷираш ҳамчун фарзанди хеш нишон додааст. Акс аз бойгонӣ Донишгоҳи омӯзгории Тоҷикистон хабари Радиои Озоди ро дар бораи ихроҷи панҷ донишҷӯяш барои сарпечӣ аз ширкат дар раҳпаймоҳои ҷашнӣ тасдиқ кард, аммо гуфт, ба се рондашуда баъди эътирофи камбудӣ иҷоза додааст, ба таҳсил баргарданд. Дар баёнияи донишгоҳ, ки 20-уми октябр дар Фейсбук нашр шуд, омадааст, “дар ҳақиқат, панҷ донишҷӯ бо сабаби риоя накардани қоидаҳои тартиботи дохилидонишгоҳӣ, аз ҷумла иштирок накардан дар корҳои ҷамъиятии донишгоҳ, аз сафи донишҷӯён хориҷ гардида буданд.” Баъди ин, ба гуфтаи раҳбарияти донишгоҳ, “бо мақсади ҳифзи ҳуқуқи донишҷӯён ва фароҳам овардани шароити мусоид барои идомаи таҳсили онҳо”, се нафар ба сафи донишҷӯён барқарор карда шуданд. Рӯзе пештар аз ин баёния, Радиои Озодӣ бо такя ба фармони раҳбарияти донишгоҳ гузориш дод, ки панҷ донишҷӯро барои иштирок накардан дар роҳпаймоӣ ё маршировка и бахшида ба ҷашни 35-солагии истиқлоли Тоҷикистон дар тобистону тирамоҳи имсол аз донишгоҳ хориҷ кардаанд . ИНЧУНИН, БИХОНЕД: "Ба маршировка наомад." Ихроҷи 5 донишҷӯ аз як донишгоҳи Тоҷикистон Ҷашни мазкур рӯзи 9-уми сентябр сурат гирифт. Вазорати маориф гуфта буд, ки ширкат дар чунин маросим маҷбурӣ нест. Хуршед Мавлонов, сухангӯи вазорат, рӯзи 20-уми октябр бори дигар тасдиқ кард, ки ширкати донишҷӯён дар раҳпаймоӣ ихтиёрист. Ҳуқуқшиноси тоҷик Бахтиёр Насруллоев дар шарҳи кӯтоҳе ба Радиои Озодӣ гуфт: "Агар донишҷӯ дар дарсҳо мунтазам иштирок накунад, имтиҳонҳоро супурда натавонад ва ё ба амалҳои ғайриқонунӣ ё ҷинояте даст занад, раҳбарияти донишгоҳ метавонад ӯро хориҷ кунад. Дигар чизҳо, ба мисли иштирок накардан дар корҳои ҷамъиятӣ ё маршировка, асос барои аз донишгоҳ хориҷ кардан намешавад." Ҷалби ҳазорон нафар бавижа хонандагону донишҷӯён дар барномаи ҷашнии 35-умин солгарди истиқлол дар Душанбе сабаби танқидҳои зиёд дар шабакаҳои иҷтимоӣ шуд. Корбарон дар Фейсбук ва Инстаграм мегуфтанд, ки донишгоҳҳо ба ҷойи дарс додан ба донишҷӯён, онҳоро барои рақсу бозӣ мефиристанд. Мунтақидони маршировка бовар доранд, ки чунин маъракаҳо дар Тоҷикистон аз даврони шӯравии собиқ ба мерос мондаанд ва бояд ҳарчи зудтар аз он даст кашид. Маъракаҳое, ки ба гуфтаи онҳо даврони шахспарастӣ, саркӯб ва поймоли ҳуқуқу озодиҳои бунёдии мардумро ба ёд меоваранд. Донишгоҳи омӯзгории Тоҷикистон гуфтааст, ихроҷи панҷ донишҷӯ “хусусияти ислоҳӣ дошта, ҳадафи асосии он ҷалби таваҷҷуҳи донишҷӯён ба масъулиятшиносӣ, ислоҳи камбудиҳо ва риояи талаботи тартиботи донишгоҳ буд.” Ҳарчанд донишгоҳ гуфтааст, ки барои ширкаткунандагони раҳпаймоии идона 10 рӯз рухсатӣ дод, намояндаи Вазорати маориф ва илми Тоҷикистон мегӯяд, барои ин қишри донишҷӯён ҳеч гуна таътили иловагӣ эълон накардааст.
