https://www.rferl.org/a/rubio-ukraine-pe.body: News Rubio Vows To Keep Pushing For Ukraine Peace, Seeks Deeper US Ties In Central Asia By Alex Raufoglu October 19, 2026 11:29 CET Rubio Vows To Keep Pushing For Ukraine Peace, Seeks Deeper US Ties In Central Asia Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google US Secretary of State Marco Rubio (right) meets with Kazakh Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, on October 19. SAMARKAND -- US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Washington would continue efforts to end Russia's war against Ukraine, warning that the conflict risks escalating beyond the two countries as he met with Central Asian officials in Uzbekistan. Speaking to reporters in Samarkand on October 19, Rubio defended President Donald Trump's push for negotiations with Moscow and Kyiv, acknowledged limited progress, and said Washington remained open to any opportunity to secure a settlement. “No one's winning that war,” Rubio said. “People are dying every day. Things are being blown up every day. Things are being destroyed every day.” Rubio's visit, which brought nearly 300 American business representatives to Uzbekistan, also highlighted Washington's efforts to expand economic ties with Central Asia, a region where China has become the leading trading partner while Russia retains longstanding security and economic links. SEE ALSO: Rubio Heads To Central Asia As US Seeks Bigger Role In Region Dominated By Russia, China Meeting with the foreign ministers of Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Uzbekistan under the C5+1 framework, Rubio said the US wanted to strengthen its presence without demanding that regional governments choose between competing powers. Asked about reports that Russian President Vladimir Putin had proposed a meeting with Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to discuss ending the war, Rubio said discussions about a possible meeting had taken place but that he did not believe all arrangements had been finalized. Trump remained committed to ending the conflict, Rubio said, adding that Washington would continue testing opportunities for negotiations despite the lack of progress so far. “This is not a criminal case,” Rubio said when asked what evidence the administration had that Putin was serious about peace talks. “This is about diplomacy, and in diplomacy, you continue to try.” He said a deal would ultimately depend on whether both sides were willing to make concessions. Rubio: Dangers Beyond Ukraine Rubio also defended the administration's decision to suspend certain sanctions for 60 days, saying it was intended to give ongoing talks with Russia and Ukraine a chance to produce results. He cited the war's mounting human and economic costs, referring to Trump's repeated claim that as many as 25,000 people are dying each month in the fighting. Rubio warned that the conflict posed dangers beyond Ukraine and Russia, particularly for Eastern Europe. Drones disrupted by electronic warfare, failed sabotage operations, and other incidents could cause damage in neighboring countries and risk triggering a wider confrontation, he said. The US wanted to bring the war to an end because of both its devastating consequences and the risk of escalation, Rubio added. SEE ALSO: Rubio Warns Russia's War Could Spill Beyond Ukraine's Borders Asked about Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's assertion that Washington had temporarily paused some intelligence sharing with Kyiv before resuming it, Rubio said there had been no interruption. “I don't know where he's getting these things from or why he's saying these things to the press,” Rubio said. He also declined to comment on reports that Ukraine had not received advance warning before Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv, saying he did not know the details of that incident. He acknowledged that US officials had examined a software problem involving Ukraine's early-warning system in an earlier episode. Rubio said Washington had not changed its diplomatic presence in Kyiv, although the safety of US diplomats and facilities remained a concern. Asked whether relations between the Trump and Zelenskyy administrations had fundamentally broken down, Rubio said Washington's priority was to end the war. He acknowledged that Ukraine wanted to expand its use of the Starshield satellite communications system, which is controlled by the US Department of War, to conduct attacks beyond Ukrainian territory. He declined to discuss those negotiations further. US Seeks To Compete With China Rubio's visit also underscored Washington's ambition to gain a stronger economic foothold in Central Asia, where China is the principal trading partner of all five countries. Chinese companies have secured deals involving regional energy resources and minerals, while Russia remains connected to the region through pipelines, security arrangements, and labor migration. Moscow's invasion of Ukraine has encouraged Central Asian governments to diversify their international relationships. Asked how the US intended to compete with China, Rubio said Washington was seeking a fair opportunity for American businesses rather than asking regional governments to sever existing ties. “This is not about coming here to say stop talking to somebody else or stop working with some other country,” he said. Rubio said the US delegation had come to identify investment and trade opportunities, with agreements worth billions of dollars expected to be announced. Uzbekistan, he added, wanted to maintain relationships with multiple powers. “They want to be friends to everybody,” Rubio said of the Uzbek government. “They want to have a relationship with everybody.” SEE ALSO: As Russian Arms Exports Slide, Central Asia Shops Elsewhere He described Uzbekistan as a key regional player, citing its population, economic development, and tourism potential. Rubio said the country's reported annual economic growth of nearly 8 percent offered significant opportunities for further cooperation. He also called for greater US engagement with Central Asia, saying the region had not received the attention it deserved from American policymakers over the past two decades. The visit was intended to establish a foundation for longer-term cooperation, Rubio said, rather than simply produce a series of immediate commercial agreements. Critical Minerals And Energy Security Rubio also highlighted the importance of diversifying global supply chains, particularly for critical minerals used in advanced technologies and industries. “It's just not smart for the whole world to depend on one place for 100 percent of anything,” he said, arguing that excessive dependence on a single supplier left countries vulnerable to political tensions and disruptions. Countries with critical minerals and the ability to process them, he said, had an economic interest in developing those resources responsibly. Washington was interested in partnerships that could benefit local economies while diversifying supplies for American and global industries. SEE ALSO: Trump Defends Russia Sanctions Waivers, Zelenskyy Says Kyiv Attacked Without Early Warning From Partners On energy, Rubio defended the administration's use of sanctions waivers affecting Russian oil supplies, rejecting the suggestion that the measures meant Washington had changed its position on purchases of Russian energy. He said decisions had to take into account global prices, energy availability, and the economic circumstances of individual countries, including their ability to find alternative suppliers. “It's not solely dominated by” the war in Ukraine, Rubio said of US foreign policy, adding that bilateral relationships and broader economic considerations also mattered. He said Washington was close to a trade deal with India, another factor in the administration's calculations as it sought to balance energy policy and geopolitical priorities. Rubio Backs Jac

https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-russia-t.body: Ukraine Trump Defends Russia Sanctions Waivers, Zelenskyy Says Kyiv Attacked Without Early Warning From Partners By RFE/RL October 19, 2026 00:52 CET Trump Defends Russia Sanctions Waivers, Zelenskyy Says Kyiv Attacked Without Early Warning From Partners Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Employees check medicines at a damaged pharmacy near a metro station that was hit during a Russian missile strike on Kyiv overnight on October 19. President Donald Trump slammed his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelenskyy and defended his decision to waive sweeping sanctions planned against Russia as an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table amid strong criticism from Kyiv and some US lawmakers that it sends the wrong message to the Kremlin. In a social media post on October 18, Trump blamed Zelenskyy for a lack of willingness to end Russia's war against his country, claiming that he "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did." Following Trump's latest war of words against the Ukrainian leader, volleys of Russian ballistic and cruise missiles and attack drones struck targets in Kyiv and other parts of the country, killing at least two people and injuring several others. Zelenskky noted that Russia had damaged more than 10 energy facilities in overnight attacks, leaving more than half a million people without electricity as "once again, there was no early warning from our partners." Ukraine's military later said the first wave of strikes came without warning, while alerts about a second wave were received. Last week Kyiv also said there had been no warning from the United States of similar strikes, leaving little time for residents to take shelter. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, attending a meeting of Central Asian countries in Uzbekistan, denied on October 19 that there had been any suspension of intelligence sharing with Ukraine. "There has been no pause," Rubio told reporters in Uzbekistan when asked about Ukraine's claims, calling on Zelensky to "focus" on ending the war with Russia. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that Russian attacks on the capital killed a 21-year-old woman, injured several people, damaged residential buildings, a metro station, and a medical center, while no patients were present at the facility at the time of the strike. Russian military confirmed a strike on Kyiv and the surrounding region, claiming it targeted military-industrial facilities, missile and drone storage sites, and a data processing center. Trump signed an executive order late on October 16 that waives new sanctions mandated by legislation named for the late US senator Lindsey Graham, an ardent supporter of Ukraine, days after giving temporary relief on Russian diesel sanctions. Trump signed last month at the urging of lawmakers who want to pressure Moscow over its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, launched in February 2022. But the moves in recent days to ease sanctions have sparked fierce criticism from many corners that Trump was giving the Kremlin a chance to fund its war machine, an accusation the president rejected. "I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine, and don't want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table," Trump wrote on Truth Social on October 18. Trump made ending Russia's war on Ukraine war a priority when he began his current term in January 2025, but Kyiv and Moscow remain far apart in their negotiating positions and talks have stalled. The Kremlin has been offering no concessions, repeatedly rejecting calls for a full cease-fire, and sticking to demands including Russian control over the territory it has been unable to seize in battle. The stalemate has seen the two sides step up attacks, with Moscow pummeling Kyiv and other major cities, along with targeting energy infrastructure, wreaking havoc on utilities just as Ukraine prepares for winter. Ukraine's armed forces, in return, have targeted Russia's refining operations to hinder its military operations. Those strikes have angered Trump, whose Republican party is engaged in a tight battle for control of both the Senate and House amid surging fuel prices that have angered many voters. SEE ALSO: Ukrainian Officials Slam Trump's Waiver Of Russia Sanctions As Rubio Defends Move Zelenskyy warned of dire consequences for Ukraine if US support disappears. "If the United States will take the side of Russia, of course we will not prevail," Zelenskyy told the NBC news show "Meet the Press" on October 18. "We want to trust him, and I hope that he will change his decisions...Because I think that it's all mistakes and it will not help us. And it will not help United States." He added that intelligence-sharing that Ukraine said had been interrupted earlier this week now appears to have been "de-blocked." "We are very thankful for this," Zelenskyy said. "Now it works." SEE ALSO: Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule A week ago, as Trump unilaterally announced an energy cease-fire on social media, Zelenskyy appeared to support halting the strikes but said he expected Moscow to do the same. However, as Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy sites continued, the Ukrainian president said Kyiv was "done" with unilaterally pausing its own. There was no indication Moscow had supported cease-fire announced by Trump. Putin, who Russian media said was visiting a command post earlier in the week, ordered the Russian military to continue its "massive and coordinated" strikes against targets in Ukraine. Trump's easing of sanctions has met with disdain from many lawmakers on both sides of the aisle in the United States, as well as from Ukraine's international partners. While Trump administration officials including US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended the president's actions, Republican lawmaker Don Bacon said moves helping the Kremlin "will go down as a very embarrassing chapter in U.S. history." SEE ALSO: Zelenskyy Says Russia Seeking Blackout In Ukraine After Latest Onslaught On Energy Facilities Trump's latest comments highlighted the growing tensions between Washington and Kyiv over the administration's approach to Russia. Zelenskyy earlier announced he had held talks with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. He added that Ukraine and the United States were "preparing the next steps in diplomacy" and that his country remained "ready to work constructively, honestly, and toward a real result." "Peace comes only through strength and cooperation built on trust," Zelenskyy said in a social media post about the talks. "We are doing everything on our part to make this happen, and to ensure that America’s position is strong and helps bring peace closer. Peace that everyone, except Russia, has been waiting for over the past four and a half years." https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2.body: Initial reports suggest that the police deployed excessive force to disperse a peaceful protest camp in Porto, Portugal, in the early hours of 15 October that injured 37 people, said Amnesty International in a statement today. “Reports of police violence against people peacefully protesting Portugal’s housing crisis are deeply troubling. People have the right to protest peacefully, including the right to occupy public space and including at night-time. The Portuguese authorities must respect and protect that right. “Dispersal of peaceful protests must be a last resort. Reports that police beat protesters with batons resulting in dozens of people being injured, including a person with a disability, raise serious concerns that the use of force was disproportionate,” said João Godinho Martins, Executive Director of Amnesty International Portugal. Reports that police beat protesters with batons resulting in dozens of people being injured, including a person with a disability, raise serious concerns that the use of force was disproportionate.” João Godinho Martins, Executive Director of Amnesty International Portugal On 10 October, people started to gather in Porto’s Praça D. João I to protest against the unaffordability of housing in Portugal, inspired by protests in Spain following the eviction of Maricarmen Abascal . Protestors initially set up 50 tents to occupy the square and, according to media reports, described the peaceful action as “an act of political desperation”. On the morning of 12 October, Portuguese police ordered protesters to remove tents, citing an “unauthorized occupation of public property”. Police subsequently removed and confiscated the tents and belongings, according to protesters in contact with Amnesty International. The protest continued and on 12 October the activists notified Porto City Council of their intention to continue their demonstration. Porto mayor Pedro Duarte responded by saying that he would take an “absolutely uncompromising” stance against attempts to set up tents in the square. At around 2.30am on 15 October, roughly 40 police officers arrived at Praça D. João I to disperse the protest. Portuguese law includes a problematic blanket ban on night-time protests that runs contrary to the right to protest. According to activists and their lawyers, the police intervention resulted in 35 people sustaining minor injuries and two people sustaining serious injuries, including head injuries, a broken arm and a broken wrist. A person with a disability was among those injured. Portuguese media also reported that several people were taken to hospital. The Porto fire service reportedly assisted eight people in total and transferred two to hospital. Tomás Varela, a protester who received treatment at Santo António Hospital, reported being struck on the head with a baton and requiring nine stitches. The police described the operation as a “heavy-handed intervention” and said it was prompted by protesters’ resistance to removing the tents. “From evidence we have verified online and from interviewing protesters and witnesses at the scene, Amnesty International is concerned that the Portuguese police used excessive (and thus unlawful) force against peaceful protesters. “The Portuguese authorities must ensure an independent, impartial and effective investigation into the police operation. Anyone found responsible for unlawful use of force must be held accountable. The authorities must also fully protect the right to protest, including at night-time,” said João Godinho Martins. Background Portugal is one of the European countries most affected by the housing crisis. House prices hit a new high in 2025 , and were the highest in the eurozone. In Lisbon, the share of salary spent on rent is 116% meaning rent surpasses the average salary by 16%. Access to affordable housing continues to be a serious and persistent problem, with almost 13% of the Portuguese population living in overcrowded households . The right to housing is enshrined in Article 65 of the Portuguese Constitution which states that “everyone has the right, for themselves and their family, to housing of an adequate size, in conditions of hygiene and comfort, and which preserves personal privacy and family privacy”. The right to adequate housing is also enshrined in the International Covenant on Economic, Social, and Cultural Rights, to which Portugal is a state party. Affordability is a key component of the right to adequate housing.

The new proposals to change the ethical framework governing Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global could significantly weaken independent human rights oversight, reduce transparency and make it harder to exclude companies linked to serious abuses, Amnesty International said today. Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global, the world’s largest sovereign wealth fund, is reviewing its ethical governance framework. The Gjedrem Committee, set up for this purpose, has proposed weakening the independent Council on Ethics, allowing some of its assessments to remain confidential, and making it harder to exclude companies linked to serious human rights risks. “The proposed ethical governance changes in the Norwegian fund risk weakening accountability and integrity and dismantling key human rights protections and amount to the most significant weakening of its human rights safeguards in two decades. When the world’s largest sovereign wealth fund changes its standards, the consequences do not stop at Norway’s borders. Other investors pay attention, and companies do too,” said John Peder Egenæs, Secretary General of Amnesty International Norway. “Under the new proposals, the Council on Ethics would lose its ability to recommend exclusion, while some companies could remain in the portfolio despite serious human rights risks and failed engagement efforts. This risks weakening independent ethical scrutiny precisely when it is most needed and making certain investments too big to exclude. This is a dangerous approach and in practice imply that companies at risk of contributing to serious violations of international law are never excluded from the fund.” When the world’s largest sovereign wealth fund changes its standards, the consequences do not stop at Norway’s borders. Other investors pay attention, and companies do too. John Peder Egenæs, Secretary General of Amnesty International Norway Greater discretion demands greater scrutiny The new proposals recommend that the Council of Ethics would continue to assess the risk of companies contributing to or being responsible for serious ethical violations, but without recommending exclusion or observation. Instead, the central bank of Norway, the Norges Bank (NBIM), would determine the response. The proposals also allow the Council’s risk assessments to be withheld from public disclosure where specified conditions relating to the fund’s economic interests or NBIM’s ability to fulfil its management responsibilities are met. This is a major setback for transparency, integrity and accountability. “First, the watchdog loses its teeth. Then the curtains are drawn. The fund belongs to the Norwegian people, yet they risk losing access to information about any serious abuses that their money could be linked to,” said Egenæs. While limited confidentiality during company engagement may sometimes be justified, the public must still be able to scrutinize why NBIM retains investments in companies linked to serious human rights risks. “The Norwegian people have a right to know what the bank is asking companies to change, whether those changes are actually implemented, and why it continues to invest when serious human rights risks remain,” said Egenæs. First, the watchdog loses its teeth. Then the curtains are drawn. The fund belongs to the Norwegian people, yet they risk losing access to information about any serious abuses that their money could be linked to. John Peder Egenæs Technology suppliers’ ongoing role must be examined The Gjedrem Committee report recognizes that cloud computing, artificial intelligence and data analysis can be used in surveillance, intelligence gathering and military targeting, but proposes that sales of generic products should normally fall outside conduct-based exclusion criteria. For major technology companies, the committee states that diversification considerations may carry decisive weight when assessing exclusion. “Military use alone is insufficient to establish a company’s involvement in human rights abuses. But civilian applications cannot be used to avoid scrutiny of the role technology may play in any serious rights violations. Too often, the dual-use nature of these technologies is invoked to avoid meaningful scrutiny of the risks they create,” said Egenæs. “The fund must examine what the supplier knows, how its services are used, and what it does to prevent or stop the misuse. There is an important distinction between selling a standard product and continuing to operate, adapt and support services used in serious abuses.” Engagement cannot justify indefinite delay Under the proposed framework, engagement with the company in order to address ethical concerns would replace exclusion as the primary response when risks of serious ethical violations are identified. NBIM would be required to exclude a company only where engagement has failed or has no realistic prospect of succeeding within a reasonable time, unless exclusion would limit the fund’s ability to remain broadly diversified globally. This exception risks allowing financial considerations to override human rights concerns. It also risks weakening the fund’s leverage over companies. “An abuse does not become less serious because a company is large or an investment profitable. Applying the same ethical standard means little if the fund can retain the investment after efforts to secure change have failed,” said Egenæs. “Engagement is a tool, not an end in itself. Without a credible possibility of exclusion, engagement risks becoming a conversation without consequences. In situations of armed conflict or occupation, the urgency of protecting people must guide the response. An ongoing dialogue is not, by itself, evidence that risks are being reduced.” An abuse does not become less serious because a company is large or an investment profitable. John Peder Egenæs Weapons safeguards would be weakened The committee further proposes an exception to the nuclear weapons exclusion criterion for producers based in states that are both recognized nuclear-weapon states under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and NATO allies of Norway. This would allow certain producers based in the United States, the United Kingdom and France to become eligible for investment. “The catastrophic humanitarian consequences of nuclear weapons – the most inhumane and destructive weapons ever to be created – do not change with the nationality of their producer. Norway’s alliances must not determine which nuclear weapons producers the fund considers acceptable investments; all companies involved must be excluded,” said Egenæs. The committee also recommends removing the specific criterion addressing arms sales to states that use those weapons to commit serious and systematic violations of international humanitarian law. It proposes retaining the criterion concerning serious violations of individuals’ rights in war and conflict, and expanding a separate criterion concerning arms sales to states subject to sanctions or arms embargoes supported by Norway. “These remaining safeguards matter. But removing an explicit criterion addressing arms transfers used in serious violations of international humanitarian law risks weakening scrutiny of suppliers and the human rights impacts of their products,” said Egenæs. Amnesty International is calling on the Norwegian government and parliament to ensure and maintain strong, independent, ethical oversight of the fund, ensure meaningful public transparency and participation and preserve exclusion as a vital safeguard when engagement cannot effectively mitigate serious human rights risks. The revised framework must be grounded in the United Nations Convention against Corruption, UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises on Responsible Business Conduct, including risk-based and heightened human rights due diligence in conflict-affected settings. “Human rights and independent oversig

Reacting to the growing number of reports that peaceful activists protesting the school hijab ban have been detained and that an activist who attempted to organize free online lessons for girls affected by the uniform regulations has gone missing, Marie Struthers, Amnesty International’s Eastern Europe and Central Asia Director, said: “Mass arrests of peaceful protesters alongside participants in violent riots, including the reported detention of a mother protesting against her daughter’s exclusion from school, and the disappearance of an activist who aimed to help affected girls, are typical of the state’s violent suppression of the lawful exercise of the right to protest peacefully, and the crackdown on freedom of expression and all dissent in Azerbaijan. “Denying girls access to classrooms because they wear a hijab is discriminatory and violates their rights to education, and the freedoms of religion and expression. The secular character of public education doesn’t justify a blanket restriction on religious dress. Denying girls access to classrooms because they wear a hijab is discriminatory and violates their rights to education, and the freedoms of religion and expression Marie Struthers, Amnesty International’s Eastern Europe and Central Asia Director “The Azerbaijani authorities must reverse these discriminatory restrictions and ensure that affected pupils and teachers can return to school. They must immediately and unconditionally release anyone detained solely for peacefully exercising their rights. They must respect the right to peaceful protest and all human rights.” Background According to new school uniform regulations, from 12 October, pupils and teachers wearing hijabs were denied entry to schools across Azerbaijan, prompting mass protests and acts of public disobedience, some of them resulting in violence. On that day, according to the Interior Ministry, 37 people were detained in Baku alone, while activists reported more than 200 detentions. Simultaneously, users reported that TikTok and Instagram became inaccessible in Azerbaijan. While most of the detained were shortly released, the total number of people remaining in custody is unknown. Among the known cases is Gudrat Abdullayev, who has been placed under administrative arrest for 25 days for a TikTok post, and Rafael Huseynzade, detained for 30 days after writing “Freedom for the hijab!” on a school building. On 13 October, six minors were detained on suspicion of attempting to set fire to a school. A criminal case was opened under Article 233 of the Criminal Code, concerning the organization of actions that disrupt public order or active participation in them. Officially, no one has been arrested in connection with this case so far. On 14 October, Aga Huseynov, a Muslim activist, reported the arrest of his wife, Shahizyar Huseynova, detained the previous day after protesting outside a school in Baku after their daughter was refused access. According to him, she has been detained for four months and the charges against her have not been provided. Ilkin Huseynov, an activist who had launched a free online platform connecting volunteer teachers with children excluded from school, including for wearing hijabs, went missing on 14 October after leaving his Baku home accompanied by unidentified people.

Responding to the dramatic escalation of armed hostilities between the Huthi de facto authorities, the Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia in recent weeks and the growing toll on civilians amidst ongoing attacks, Amnesty International’s Regional Director for the Middle East and North Africa, Heba Morayef, said: “The risks to civilians in Yemen and Saudi Arabia are rapidly increasing each day this conflict escalates. All parties to the conflict must ensure civilians are protected and abide by their obligations under international humanitarian law. “Over the past week, deadly Huthi attacks on airports in Saudi Arabia have caused significant civilian harm, including a 10 October attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 13 people and wounded hundreds more- the deadliest attack in Saudi Arabia in over a decade. The attack came amidst the return of full-blown armed hostilities to Yemen with devastating consequences for civilians there, particularly on the coast and around Ta’iz, Yemen’s third largest city. Civilians are never legitimate targets. They must not pay the price of further escalation. Heba Morayef, Amnesty International “Civilians are never legitimate targets. They must not pay the price of further escalation. The deliberate targeting of civilians or civilian infrastructure, including civilian airports, is prohibited under international humanitarian law and can amount to a war crime. “All warring parties must immediately refrain from carrying out direct attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, as well as indiscriminate or disproportionate attacks. “In Yemen, where civilians are already grappling with a severe humanitarian crisis and the impact of years of sporadic bouts of fighting, the conflict will further compound the suffering of the civilian population. It is critical that parties to the conflict take all feasible precautions to avoid or, in any event, minimize harm to civilians and civilian objects, and provide unfettered access to humanitarian aid for civilians in need.” Background Recent weeks have seen a dramatic escalation in hostilities between the Huthi de-facto authorities in Yemen, the internationally recognized Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia. The renewed conflict in Yemen is linked to the regional conflict involving the US, Israel, and Iran. The Huthis are supported by Iran and the Yemeni government by Saudi Arabia. The escalation in Yemen follows the breakdown of a UN-brokered ceasefire in July 2026, following air strikes on Sana’a airport claimed by the internationally recognized government. Between 2015 and 2022, Amnesty International documented gross human rights violations and serious violations of international humanitarian law, including likely war crimes, committed by parties to the conflict, including the Huthi armed group and Saudi-led coalition. The escalation has been accompanied by intensified ground fighting between the Huthis and Yemeni government forces inside Yemen, including deadly attacks by Huthi forces on civilian areas. While the real death toll is significantly higher, the UN human rights office reported in late September that it had documented at least 32 civilians, including 15 children, killed since August. Huthi forces have also carried out attacks targeting airports, military installations and oil facilities across Saudi Arabia, as well as ships at sea. Between 5 and 11 October, Huthi attacks on civilian airports across Saudi Arabia damaged passenger terminals and civilian aircraft and killed at least 20 people and injured more than 350 people, according to the National. Saudi Arabia has also resumed its air strikes in Yemen. According to the Yemen Data Project, at least 66 civilians have been killed and 90 injured. The latest escalation is exacerbating an already severe humanitarian crisis in Yemen where, according to UN figures, at least 18.3 million people are acutely food insecure and more than 2.2 million children under five and 1.3 million pregnant and breastfeeding women are acutely malnourished. Access to food and healthcare have repeatedly worsened due to the conflict, warring party conduct and humanitarian funding cuts .

https://www.rferl.org/a/ukraine-russia-w.body: News Ukrainian Officials Slam Trump's Waiver Of Russia Sanctions As Rubio Defends Move By RFE/RL October 18, 2026 12:36 CET Ukrainian Officials Slam Trump's Waiver Of Russia Sanctions As Rubio Defends Move Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Gas prices at a Shell gas station are displayed outside of the Marathon Petroleum Corp. Los Angeles Refinery in Carson, California, on September 22. Energy analysts have questioned whether the recent diesel deal would significantly lower prices for American consumers. Ukrainian officials sharply criticized US President Donald Trump's decision to waive sweeping planned sanctions against Russia, saying that it "sends the wrong message to the aggressor" and "helps only the Russians." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the administration needed up to 60 days to assess the potential economic impact of the sanctions and tariffs, while the White House argued that imposing them immediately could hinder efforts to negotiate a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine. "If Russians are cheering yesterday's decisions in the US, it is certainly not about effective pressure to end the war," Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andriy Sybiha wrote on X on October 17. "Indecisiveness sends the wrong signal to the aggressor. It only prolongs the war." He added that "Lindsey Graham understood this well," referring to the late senator of South Carolina for whom the sanctions legislation, known as the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 -- was named. Graham, who died on July 11, was a prominent congressional supporter of Ukraine. The bill passed Congress with overwhelming bipartisan support and was signed into law by Trump in September. But in an executive order signed late on October 16, Trump said withholding the measures was in the national interest of the United States. The order came just two days before the sanctions package was due to take effect on October 18. The move prompted sharp criticism from Ukraine advocates and lawmakers from both parties who say the move undermines efforts to force Moscow to negotiate. SEE ALSO: Trump Waives Graham Act Sanctions On Russia Before They Take Effect Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said removing the sanctions "definitely helps only the Russians." "The decision to undo all of this, to block all of it, seems wrong to me," Zelenskiy wrote on X on October 17. The law was designed to give the administration additional leverage over Russian President Vladimir Putin by authorizing tariffs of up to 100 percent on major purchasers of Russian oil and gas, including China and India, and providing for sanctions targeting Russian officials, financial institutions, and the country's so-called shadow fleet of tankers used to circumvent existing restrictions. Rubio defended the White House's decision to waive new sanctions on Russia on October 17, saying Washington needed time to assess the economic consequences of additional penalties as conflicts across several regions strain global energy supplies. Speaking to reporters at Joint Base Andrews before departing for a series of diplomatic and trade talks in Central Asia, Rubio defended the administration's efforts to balance pressure on Moscow against economic concerns. The waiver followed a diesel deal Trump announced with Russia on October 9 that prompted criticism that Washington was prioritizing domestic fuel prices over efforts to constrain the Kremlin's war against Ukraine. Zelenskyy called the waiver was an unfortunate decision to backtrack on the sanctions at a time when "pressure is needed." SEE ALSO: Zelenskyy Says Russia Seeking Blackout In Ukraine After Latest Onslaught On Energy Facilities "At a time when the Russians have carried out such a massive attack on our energy sector, a decision was unfortunately made in America to completely disregard the Lindsey Graham Act, which was supposed to impose truly effective pressure on Russia to bring this war to an end," Zelenskyy wrote on X . "Russia is trying to cause a blackout in Ukraine -- right before winter," he said. "Russia is trying to leave millions of our people without electricity and heating. Pressure is needed to stop this. A U.S. sanctions blackout, easing pressure on the aggressor, financial rewards for Putin -- all of this only encourages him to keep attacking." A senior envoy to Russian President Vladimir Putin, meanwhile, praised the waiver as "a truly historic moment." Kirill Dmitriev, who heads Russia’s sovereign wealth fund, wrote on X late on October 16 that "economic cooperation between Russia and the United States serves the interest of both nations." Energy Costs Complicate Russia Sanctions Rubio said the administration needed 60 days to assess the effects of sanctions and tariffs, including their potential impact on countries such as India, which continues to rely substantially on Russian energy despite efforts to diversify its supplies. He pointed to disruptions involving Iran, the Strait of Hormuz, attacks by Yemen's Houthi movement, and the war between Russia and Ukraine as factors putting pressure on global energy markets. "These conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other," Rubio said. The United States was paying higher prices than it wanted, he said, while some other countries were approaching a crisis over energy costs and availability. Rubio also defended the administration's diesel deal with Russia -- which Zelenskyy called "a gift" to Putin -- arguing the fuel would have reached international markets regardless of whether the United States purchased it. "The only difference is how much of it the United States was going to get," he said. Energy analysts have questioned whether the deal would significantly lower prices for American consumers, while warning that easing restrictions could provide Moscow with substantial economic benefits. The waiver blocks additional sanctions and tariffs approved by Congress to discourage major purchasers of Russian oil and gas, although existing sanctions remain in place. The decision drew sharp criticism from both parties. Republican Senator Thom Tillis called it "beyond irresponsible," while Senator John Cornyn said the late senator Graham "would be appalled." Democratic lawmakers also accused Trump of helping Russia finance its war. https://www.amnesty.org/fr/latest/news/2.body: En lançant des sanctions contre la Cour pénale internationale (CPI) en tant qu’institution, le gouvernement des États-Unis cherche à détruire la Cour et à éliminer toute possibilité que les auteurs de crime de droit international soient traduits en justice, a déclaré Amnesty International vendredi 9 octobre. Les États doivent prendre toutes les mesures appropriées afin de contrer cette attaque et de protéger activement la Cour. « Les sanctions prises par le président Trump sont conçues pour isoler et, au bout du compte, détruire la Cour pénale internationale. Cette attaque existentielle doit échouer. Les États doivent prendre des mesures concrètes pour résister à l’imposition de ces mesures et protéger la Cour de manière active », a déclaré Erika Guevara Rosas, directrice générale des recherches, de l’élaboration des lignes de conduite, du travail de plaidoyer et des campagnes à Amnesty International. « La timidité des États, leurs efforts d’apaisement et leur réticence à bloquer les attaques contre la justice internationale ont enhardi les acteurs cherchant à la fragiliser. Ce moment décisif requiert courage, solidarité et action. Le combat pour la CPI est un terrain d’affrontement crucial entre ceux qui affirment que le droit doit s’incliner devant le pouvoir et que l’impunité doit être garantie aux criminels de guerre et auteurs de génocide, et ceux qui luttent pour préserver l’obligation de rendre des comptes, l’égalité face à la loi et la justice pour les victimes. Le futur de la CPI, et de la justice internationale elle-même, dépendra de la volonté des gouvernements et des peuples de la défendre. Les sanctions prises par le président Trump sont conçues pour isoler et, au bout du compte, détruire la Cour pénale internationale Erika Guevara Rosas, directrice générale des recherches, de l’élaboration des lignes de conduite, du travail de plaidoyer et des campagnes à Amnesty International « La Cour pénale internationale représente un des succès les plus important de l’ordre mondial d’après-guerre. Elle incarne une promesse simple mais vitale : que les responsables de génocide, de crimes contre l’humanité et de crimes de guerre puissent être amenés à rendre des comptes, indépendamment de leur pouvoir, de leur position ou de leur nationalité. La Cour n’est pas parfaite, mais elle constitue une voie essentielle, parfois la seule, vers l’obtention de la vérité, de la justice et de réparations. « Ces dernières années, la CPI a délivré des mandats d’arrêt contre le président russe, Vladimir Poutine, et le Premier ministre israélien, Benjamin Netanyahou. Le procès de Rodrigo Duterte, ancien président des Philippines, s’ouvrira le mois prochain. « La CPI compte 125 États membres. Ils doivent prendre des mesures concrètes pour défendre la Cour. Cela inclut un soutien politique et financier, l’adoption de « lois de blocage » nationales et régionales afin de garantir que la CPI puisse bénéficier de certains services et systèmes essentiels, la résistance face aux tentatives d’entraves à son travail, et une pleine collaboration avec ses enquêtes et ses mandats d’arrêt. « Une dernière limite a été franchie. Ceci est une attaque contre la possibilité même d’amener les personnes responsables des crimes les plus graves à répondre de leurs actes en vertu du droit international, aussi puissantes soient-elles. Il en va non seulement du futur de la Cour, mais aussi du futur de la justice internationale elle-même. De nouvelles limites doivent désormais être fixées et défendues par celles et ceux qui croient aux droits humains, au droit international et à une justice égale pour tous. « L’humanité doit triompher. »

Une coalition appelle à ce que la prochaine élection du président de la FIFA soit axée sur les droits humains La Coupe du monde masculine de 2026 a mis en évidence l’incapacité de la direction de la FIFA à mettre en œuvre ses propres politiques en matière de droits humains, la recherche de recettes record ayant été privilégiée au détriment de l’équité et de l’égalité, ont déclaré la Sport & Rights Alliance et Football Supporters Europe dans un rapport conjoint rendu public le 13 octobre. Ce rapport de 50 pages, intitulé Profit Over People: The 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, rend compte d’un tournoi marqué par un climat de peur, sur fond d’arrestations et d’expulsions massives de personnes migrantes, d’interdictions discriminatoires de visas, d’obstacles financiers et en matière d’accessibilité pour les supporteurs et supportrices, les joueurs et les journalistes, de normes de protection et d’éligibilité floues, et d’un manque d’accès effectif à des voies de recours. « La Coupe du monde 2026 a montré à quel point les priorités et l’orientation définies par la direction de la FIFA font passer le profit avant les personnes, a déclaré Andrea Florence, directrice de la Sport & Rights Alliance. « Pour toutes les personnes s’intéressant au tournoi, l’accès et la participation ont été limités par la situation économique, la nationalité, le statut migratoire, le handicap, l’identité de genre et l’orientation sexuelle, ou encore la situation politique. La FIFA, qui n’a pas utilisé son influence pour faire respecter les obligations en matière de droits humains, a en outre choisi de mettre en avant un gouvernement qui viole activement les droits fondamentaux en décernant un « Prix de la paix de la FIFA » au président américain Donald Trump. » Avec 48 nations participantes et 104 matchs disputés, la Coupe du monde masculine 2026, qui s’est tenue pour la première fois dans trois pays – le Canada, le Mexique et les États-Unis –, a été le plus grand événement sportif jamais organisé, et, comme l’avait promis la FIFA, un tournoi où chaque personne « [s’est sentie] en sécurité, incluse et libre d’exercer ses droits ». Ce tournoi a été la première Coupe du monde organisée dans le cadre de la reconnaissance et de l’adoption par la FIFA de ses obligations internationales concernant la responsabilité des entreprises en matière de droits humains, via sa politique en matière de droits humains de 2017, l’intégration de critères relatifs aux droits humains dans le processus de candidature, et un « Cadre des droits humains pour la Coupe du monde de la FIFA 2026 » dédié pour les 16 comités d’organisation locaux. Pourtant, en raison d’inquiétudes croissantes concernant d’éventuelles atteintes aux droits humains commises pendant le tournoi, plus de 65 000 personnes se sont jointes à l’appel lancé par Amnesty International pour que la FIFA et les pays hôtes s’attaquent à ces risques et garantissent une coupe du monde pour toutes et tous. Les rafles de l’ICE se sont multipliées, des manifestations ont été bloquées et les politiques discriminatoires en matière de visa ont empêché de nombreux supporteurs·trices de profiter de ce qui était présenté comme étant “la coupe du monde la plus inclusive de tous les temps” Frank Conde Tangberg, conseiller en matière de stratégie pour Amnesty International « L’unité et la joie observées sur le terrain et dans les tribunes étaient à mille lieues de la peur et des divisions régnant en dehors des stades. Les rafles de l’ICE se sont multipliées, des manifestations ont été bloquées et les politiques discriminatoires en matière de visa ont empêché de nombreux supporteurs·trices de profiter de ce qui était présenté comme étant « la coupe du monde la plus inclusive de tous les temps” », a déclaré Frank Conde Tangberg, conseiller en matière de stratégie pour Amnesty International. « Nombre de ces violations ont découlé de politiques gouvernementales répressives et abusives, mais la FIFA n’a pas usé de son influence pour protéger les supporteurs·trices et les communautés locales. Elle a utilisé son capital politique pour maximiser ses recettes plutôt que pour défendre les droits humains. » Le rapport montre de façon détaillée que les prix excessifs des billets, auxquels se sont ajoutés des formalités de visa coûteuses et à l’absence de transports interurbains abordables, ainsi que des restrictions de voyage imposées par les États-Unis pour plus de 39 pays, ont exclu de manière disproportionnée les supporteurs·trices en situation de handicap, ayant des revenus modestes et/ou venant du S ud global. Les équipes participantes et les officiels ont été confrontés à de graves perturbations. Les membres de l’équipe nationale iranienne ont ainsi vu leurs visas pour les États-Unis retardés ou refusés, et pour deux matchs aux États-Unis, l’équipe a dû entrer et sortir du pays le même jour ; et l’arbitre somalien Omar Artan, qui disposait pourtant d’un visa valide, s’est vu refuser l’entrée dans le pays à l’aéroport international de Miami après un interrogatoire ayant duré 11 heures. Ces obstacles, et d’autres encore, se sont accompagnés d’une action agressive des services d’immigration états-uniens : Human Rights Watch a ainsi réuni des informations montrant que le Service américain de l’immigration et des douanes (ICE) a procédé à plus de 167 000 arrestations dans 11 villes hôtes de la coupe du monde et à leur périphérie, à l’approche du tournoi. Bien que les informations faisant état d’arrestations opérées par l’ICE à l’intérieur des sites de la coupe du monde aient été limitées, les opérations se sont intensifiées durant le tournoi, notamment pendant cinq jours fin juin où environ 10 000 personnes ont été arrêtées. « Les supporteurs·trices ont été traités comme des sujets à exploiter plutôt que comme le cœur même du jeu, a déclaré Ronan Evain, directeur de Football Supporters Europe. « Lorsque les prix des billets atteignent des sommets sans précédent dans l’histoire de la coupe du monde, que les exigences légales en matière d’accessibilité pour les supporteurs·trices en situation de handicap ne sont pas respectées, et que des supporteurs·trices fidèles se heurtent à des refus de visa discriminatoires ou à des contrôles frontaliers militarisés, on n’est plus en présence d’une fête mondiale, mais simplement d’un spectacle luxueux et aseptisé destiné uniquement à l’élite. » Le rapport fait également état d’autres violations des droits humains commises au Mexique, où la police a réprimé des manifestations pourtant programmées en utilisant du gaz lacrymogène et arrêté deux journalistes. Au Canada, les préparatifs ont été marqués dans les villes hôtes par des opérations de nettoyage des rues avec le déplacement des personnes sans domicile fixe, et les autorités d’immigration ont rejeté plus de demandes de visa pour la coupe du monde, déposées pour la plupart par des personnes de pays du Sud global, qu’elles n’en ont acceptées. En ce qui concerne le contrôle exercé directement par la FIFA, des questions subsistent quant à savoir si elle s’est abstenue d’appliquer sa propre politique concernant les compétitions, qui exige explicitement des athlètes qu’ils déclarent n’avoir jamais fait l’objet d’une enquête pour une infraction sexuelle ou d’autres actes de violence, étant donné qu’au moins huit joueurs faisant l’objet de procédures en cours ou d’allégations d’agression sexuelle ont participé à la Coupe du monde 2026. Le journalisme indépendant a également été fortement entravé par la procédure opaque d’accréditation des médias mise en place par la FIFA, par les obstacles concernant les visas états-uniens et par l’absence de conférences de presse régulières avec les plus haut·e·s dirigeant·e·s. « Ces dernières années, les États-Unis – le pays ayant accueilli la majorité des matchs de la coupe du monde – sont passés de la 45 e à la 64 e place de notre classement mondial de la liberté de la presse, et les journalistes ont été en butte à des violences, des arrestations et de

Lorsque l’Africa Corps a officiellement pris ses fonctions au Mali en juin 2025, rares étaient ceux qui avaient l’espoir que cela allait contribuer à atténuer les souffrances des populations civiles maliennes, causées d’un côté par les groupes armés de l’Azawad ou du GSIM, mais aussi par l’armée et ses supplétifs de la société militaire privée russe, connue sous le nom de Wagner. Les troupes de l’Africa Corps, placées directement sous le contrôle du Kremlin, avaient déjà commencé à se déployer dans le pays depuis janvier 2025, et à reprendre progressivement les activités de Wagner, en soutien aux opérations militaires de l’armée. Les patrouilles conjointes de l’armée et de Wagner entre 2023 et 2025 ont été émaillées de graves exactions que nous avons de nouveau détaillées récemment dans un rapport et dont certaines s’apparentent selon nous à des crimes de guerre. LISEZ NOTRE RAPPORT : « Nul n’est épargné » : Crimes de guerre commis par l’armée malienne et les forces armées etrangères le long de la frontière mauritanienne Nous relatons notamment sept incidents au cours desquels 34 personnes ont été délibérément tuées lors de ces patrouilles. Les victimes, toutes civiles selon les témoignages recueillis, ont été tuées par balles, égorgées et brûlées, ou encore mutilées post-mortem pour certaines d’entre elles. Nombre d’entre elles ont été abattues de sang-froid, alors qu’elles étaient en train de faire paître leurs troupeaux ou après avoir été appréhendées. Témoignages de tortures systématiques Des attaques meurtrières de drones à Ejdeir (sans avertissement et un jour de foire, 16 morts) et Tangata (la nuit sur une maison, un lendemain de mariage, 7 morts), en mars et novembre 2025, ont également causé des morts et des destructions. Ces deux frappes ont été menées sans aucune preuve apparente de la présence de combattants armés ou d’objectif militaire sur ces deux sites . Si cela était confirmé, elles constitueraient des attaques directes contre des civil·e·s et des biens de caractère civil, et devraient faire l’objet d’enquêtes en tant que possibles crimes de guerre. Les tortures et mauvais traitements étaient également un fait commun lors de ces opérations. Ainsi que dans les camps militaires de Léré et de Nampala où les individus arrêtés peuvent rester des mois sans pouvoir notifier leurs familles ou être présentées devant un juge, ou simplement disparaitre. Des survivants de ces tortures assortis d’interrogatoires sur l’activité des groupes armés, et dont les corps en portent parfois encore les traces, ont parlé à Amnesty International. Suspension par les bras, simulations de noyades, électrocutions, coups de bottes et de crosse, de barres de fer, détention dans des conditions dégradantes dans des toilettes insalubres : l’éventail des pratiques est large. Certains avaient été soumis à des violences sexuelles, forcés à se déshabiller et à rester nus plusieurs jours au cours de leur détention. Des sévices commis par les éléments de Wagner pour l’essentiel mais en pleine connaissance des forces armées maliennes. Au moins cinq personnes sont mortes des suites de ces tortures selon les témoignages recueillis. La protection des populations civiles dans le cadre du conflit doit être une priorité des autorités maliennes et de toutes les parties au conflit. Ousmane Diallo, Chercheur senior sur le Sahel à Amnesty International Ce sont les membres des communautés peule, touarègue et arabe vivant le long de cette frontière avec la Mauritanie qui ont été les principales victimes des crimes de guerre documentés dans ce rapport. Parce qu’elles sont “suspectées” par l’armée et les membres du groupe Wagner d’être en collusion ou de sympathiser avec le GSIM. Parce qu’elles vivent en zone rurale, dans un espace de conflit entre les parties belligérantes. Aux crimes s’ajoutaient d’autres crimes. Les opérations militaires souvent meurtrières s’accompagnent de pillages (argent, bétail, collier, bijoux, couvertures, etc) et de destructions de biens, remettant clairement en cause les affirmations des autorités maliennes selon lesquelles elles ne ciblent que les membres de groupes armés. Alors qu’Africa Corps a remplacé Wagner, rien n’a été fait pour que la situation ne change. L’impunité demeure. Aucune poursuite judiciaire n’a été ouverte à notre connaissance sur les exactions commises par les forces gouvernementales sur des civiles depuis 2023. Les victimes n’osent pas porter plainte de peur de représailles. Ceux qui osent critiquer la conduite des opérations militaires sont victimes de répression. Les autorités militaires exercent un contrôle total sur l’information. Rencontrez trois journalistes du Sahel central, muselés par les autorités militaires Déjà, des allégations d’exactions sont portées sur les membres d’Africa Corps. Selon Human Rights Watch. Le 10 juillet 2026 à Bombori, le quartier peul du village a été investi, 80 hommes rassemblés dehors avant d’être battus et interrogés sur les activités des groupes armés. Six personnes qui tentaient de fuir ont été abattues alors que trois autres ont été exécutées. L’horreur ne doit pas succéder à l’horreur. La protection des populations civiles dans le cadre du conflit doit être une priorité des autorités maliennes et de toutes les parties au conflit, conformément au droit international humanitaire. Les opérations et camps militaires doivent être contrôlés et la justice doit pouvoir ouvrir des enquêtes indépendantes sur tout cas d’allégation d’exactions. Cet article a été publié initialement par Jeune Afrique.

En réaction à l’exécution arbitraire par les autorités iraniennes de cinq hommes – Ali Hemmati Sistanian, Alireza Raisi, Alireza Sepahi, Majid Nikandish et Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi – en l’espace d’une semaine, entre le 30 septembre et le 5 octobre, condamnés dans le cadre des manifestations de janvier 2026 à l’issue de procès manifestement iniques entachés d’actes de torture, Diana Eltahawy, directrice régionale adjointe pour le Moyen-Orient et l’Afrique du Nord à Amnesty International, a déclaré : « L’exécution arbitraire de ces cinq jeunes hommes rappelle avec effroi que les autorités iraniennes instrumentalisent la peine de mort : le prix à payer pour toute dissidence est si élevé que l’objectif est de terroriser la population afin de la faire taire et de la dissuader de se soulever collectivement pour contester le régime répressif en place depuis des décennies. « Ces exécutions font suite à des informations qui mettent en évidence un schéma effrayant et courant : l’accusé·e n’a pas la possibilité de consulter un avocat durant les interrogatoires, ses allégations de torture et de mauvais traitements ne font délibérément pas l’objet d’enquêtes, il ou elle est fréquemment inculpé·e d’être impliqué dans l’homicide de membres des forces de sécurité et dans d’autres actes violents et non violents commis lors de manifestations, ses « aveux » forcés sont diffusés à la télévision à titre d’éléments de preuve, et son procès se déroule devant des tribunaux révolutionnaires iniques par nature. C’est le cas d’Alireza Sepahi, qui a indiqué avoir subi des actes de torture et des mauvais traitements, et s’est vu refuser tout contact avec un avocat lors des interrogatoires pendant la phase d’enquête. De telles procédures tournent la justice en dérision et révèlent le mépris total des autorités iraniennes pour le droit à la vie. « De nombreux dissident·e·s et manifestant·e·s, entre autres, restent exposés au risque d’exécutions motivées par des considérations politiques, alors que les autorités intensifient la répression en invoquant une » situation de guerre » et des menaces pesant sur la sécurité nationale. Il est donc d’autant plus urgent d’exercer une pression diplomatique coordonnée sur l’Iran afin de bloquer toutes les exécutions prévues. « L’impunité systémique encourage les autorités iraniennes à poursuivre leurs atteintes au droit à la vie et aux droits fondamentaux en général ; aussi est-il urgent que le Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies saisisse la Cour pénale internationale de la situation en Iran, et que l’Assemblée générale de l’ONU établisse un mécanisme international de justice pénale pour l’Iran. » Contexte Alireza Raisi et Alireza Sepahi ont été exécutés à Ispahan le 5 octobre 2026. Selon l’agence de presse Mizan , aile médiatique du pouvoir judiciaire, ils ont été jugés lors du procès collectif dans l’affaire de la place Alikhani, dans le cadre duquel les prévenu·e·s étaient accusés d’avoir commis divers actes violents et non violents lors des manifestations qui ont eu lieu à Ispahan le 8 janvier 2026 – blocages de rues, destructions de biens, incendies volontaires et implication dans la mort de quatre membres des forces de sécurité. Ces hommes ont été condamnés à mort à l’issue d’un procès manifestement inique : leurs « aveux » forcés ont été diffusés par les médias d’État le 23 janvier, avant même l’ouverture de leur procès. Amnesty International a appris qu’Alireza Sepahi avait été soumis à des actes de torture et à des mauvais traitements pendant sa détention : maintien prolongé à l’isolement, passage à tabac et décharges électriques notamment. Selon l’agence de presse Mizan , ces hommes ont été condamnés à mort pour « rébellion armée contre l’État » ( baghi ), « inimitié à l’égard de Dieu » ( moharebeh ) pour avoir brandi des armes et semé la peur, la terreur et l’insécurité aux alentours, et « corruption sur terre » ( efsad-e fel arz ) pour avoir commis des actes portant atteinte à l’intégrité physique des personnes et à la sécurité nationale, qui ont gravement perturbé l’ordre public et engendré une insécurité généralisée, incitation à la guerre et au meurtre, ainsi que d’autres actes criminels, notamment contre la sécurité nationale. Cinq autres hommes condamnés dans le cadre de la même affaire ont déjà été exécutés et au moins huit autres risquent de l’être. Majid Nikandish et Ali Hemmati Sistanian ont été mis à mort le 30 septembre 2026 à Meched, dans la province du Khorassan Razavi. Selon l’agence de presse Mizan ,ils étaient accusés de divers actes violents et non violents lors des manifestations qui se sont déroulées à Meched le 8 janvier 2026 et que les autorités ont qualifiées de « coup d’État » – blocages de rues, destructions de biens, incendies volontaires et implication dans la mort de quatre membres des forces de sécurité notamment. Leurs « aveux » forcés diffusés à la télévision, notamment recueillis sur les lieux de leur arrestation et lors des interrogatoires qui ont suivi, en l’absence d’un avocat, ont été invoqués à titre de preuves pour les déclarer coupables et les condamner à mort. Selon Iran Human Rights , organisation indépendante de défense des droits humains basée hors d’Iran, Majid Nikandish a subi actes de torture et mauvais traitements. Il a été maintenu à l’isolement prolongé et suspendu par les bras, ce qui lui a valu une épaule déboîtée et la mâchoire cassée. Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi a été exécuté le 3 octobre 2026 à Shahrekord, dans la province du Tchaharmahal-et-Bakhtiari. Selon l’agence de presse Mizan ,il a été reconnu coupable et condamné à mort dans le cadre des manifestations qui ont eu lieu le 8 janvier à Shahrekord, pour les chefs d’accusation suivants : « inimitié à l’égard de Dieu » ( moharebeh ) pour avoir brandi une arme et ouvert le feu, et « rassemblement et collusion en vue de commettre des crimes contre la sécurité nationale ». Amnesty International n’a cessé de dénoncer le recours à ce dernier chef d’accusation à l’encontre de manifestant·e·s, de dissident·e·s et de défenseur·e·s des droits humains ayant pris part à des manifestations et des rassemblements. Les « aveux » extorqués à Siavash Jamshidi Kheirabadi ont été diffusés à la télévision et retenus à titre de preuves afin de le déclarer coupable et de le condamner à mort. Les autorités iraniennes ont exécuté au moins 34 personnes en lien avec le soulèvement de janvier 2026, au cours duquel les forces de sécurité ont massivement recouru à la force meurtrière illégale, tuant des milliers de manifestant·e·s et de passant·e·s les 8 et 9 janvier. Les exécutions à caractère politique se sont encore intensifiées à la suite des attaques illégales menées par les États-Unis et Israël contre l’Iran le 28 février 2026, tandis que les mises à mort pour des infractions liées aux stupéfiants et d’autres crimes se poursuivaient. Amnesty International s’oppose catégoriquement à la peine de mort, pour toutes les infractions et en toutes circonstances.

En réaction à l’annonce selon laquelle le gouvernement de Donald Trump a fixé la date de la première exécution militaire depuis 1961, qui se fera par peloton d’exécution et sera diffusée en direct, Justin Mazzola, directeur adjoint de la recherche à Amnesty International États-Unis, a déclaré : « L’annonce du gouvernement de Donald Trump au sujet de la première exécution militaire depuis plus de 60 ans est répréhensible et illustre le caractère arbitraire inhérent à la peine de mort, ainsi que le mépris total des autorités à l’égard du droit à la vie. « La peine de mort est une violation des droits humains, quelles que soient les circonstances. Les organismes internationaux de défense des droits humains considèrent depuis longtemps que les exécutions publiques sont incompatibles avec l’interdiction des peines ou traitements cruels, inhumains ou dégradants. L’affirmation selon laquelle la peine de mort a un effet dissuasif particulier sur la criminalité est tout simplement infondée : aucun élément ne permet de le prouver. Ce châtiment n’améliore pas notre sécurité. « Diffuser en direct la mise à mort d’une personne par un peloton d’exécution ne fera qu’aggraver la cruauté de la peine de mort et perpétuer le cycle de violence que les autorités prétendent vouloir enrayer. « Cette annonce vient s’ajouter à la cruauté dont nous venons d’être témoins dans le cadre de l’acharnement lors de l’exécution de Christa Pike dans le Tennessee. Le système de la peine de mort aux États-Unis est irrémédiablement brisé. Il est grand temps que les autorités états-uniennes, à tous les niveaux, usent de leur pouvoir afin de faire preuve de leadership en matière de droits humains et de mettre un terme définitif à ce châtiment des plus cruels, inhumains et dégradants qui soient. » Contexte Le gouvernement fédéral des États-Unis a annoncé qu’il a l’intention de procéder le 3 décembre à l’exécution d’un homme déclaré coupable du meurtre de 13 personnes lors d’une tuerie sur la base militaire de Fort Hood, au Texas, en 2009. Le 8 octobre, le secrétaire d’État à la défense, Pete Hegseth, a déclaré que cette exécution serait diffusée au public en direct. Amnesty International s’oppose en toutes circonstances et sans aucune exception à la peine de mort, quelles que soient la nature et les circonstances du crime commis, la culpabilité ou l’innocence ou toute autre situation du condamné, ou la méthode utilisée par l’État pour procéder à l’exécution. Elle milite en faveur de l’abolition totale de ce châtiment.

Самарқанда жүрген Марко Рубио не деді? АҚШ мемлекеттік хатшысы Марко Рубио Самарқанда мәлімдеме жасап, Вашингтон Ресейдің Украинаға қарсы соғысын аяқтауға деген талпынысын жалғастыратынын, соғыс ауқымы ұлғайып, аймақтық қақтығыс ұласу қаупі барын айтты. Мемлекеттік хатшы Өзбекстанның тарихи қаласында Орталық Азия елдерінің сыртқы істер министрлерімен жеке және ортақ форматта кездесу өткізіп жатыр. Рубионың баспасөз пулында Азаттық тілшісі Алекс Рауфоглу да бар. 19 қазан күні журналистер алдына шыққан Марко Рубио АҚШ президенті Дональд Трамптың Мәскеу мен Киевті келіссөздер үстеліне отырғызу әрекетін қорғап, әзірге айтарлықтай ілгерілеу болмағанын мойындады. Соған қарамастан, Вашингтон қақтығысты реттеуге мүмкіндік беретін кез келген жолды қарастыруға дайын екенін айтты. "Бұл соғыста ешкім жеңіп жатқан жоқ. Күн сайын адамдар қаза тауып жатыр. https://www.azattyq.org/a/zhaparov-ablya.body: ЖАҢАЛЫҚТАР Жапаров Әблязовтың ақша туралы айтқанын жоққа шығарды 19 қазан 2026 жыл, 15:02 Жапаров Әблязовтың ақша туралы айтқанын жоққа шығарды Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу Бөлісу Сілтемесін көшіру Facebook X (Twitter) WhatsApp Email Бөлісу PDF VPN-сіз оқу Сайт бұғатталып тұрса да, материалды осы сілтемемен кіріп оқуға болады Google-да басымдық бер Қырғызстан президенті Садыр Жапаров Қырғызстан президенті Садыр Жапаров қазақстандық оппозиционер Мұхтар Әблязовтың "Шумкар" атты қозғалыстың YouTube-арнасында айтқан сөздеріне жауап берді. Бұл туралы бүгін Азаттықтың Қырғыз қызметі хабарлады . 17 қазанда осы арнаға сұхбатында Әблязов Жапаровпен таныс екенін және 2020 жылғы қазандағы оқиғалар кезінде өзінен Жапаров ақша сұрағанын айтқан. Жапаров SUPER.KG порталының сауалдарына берген жауабында Әблязовтың бұл айтқанын терістеді. Жапаров қазақ оппозиционерімен бұрын-соңды таныс болмағанын, онымен 2020 жылғы қазан оқиғалары кезінде қасында жүрген, қазір түрмеде отырған Мелис Аспеков сөйлестіргенін айтты. "Алаяқ болса айта береді де. Ол кезде 40 минут емес, 4 минут сөйлесуге де уақытым жоқ еді. Ақша сұрады дегені – шылғи өтірік. Өзі қайыр тілеп, Франциядағы жеке өмірі үшін қазақ халқынан теңге сұрап жүрген қайыршыдан мен "ақша сұрады" дегенге кім сенеді? Қайыршыдан ақша сұрады деген қисынға да сыймайды ғой. Революция болған. Билік басына әлдеқашан келіп отырғам. Ол күндері ақшаның керегі де жоқ болатын. Түрмеден шығарып әкеліп, президент тағына отырғызған елдің ақшасыз-ақ сайлап қоятыны белгілі еді. Сондықтан суайттар, алаяқтар бірдеңе десе, сеніп қала бермеңіздер. Олар "бұтына жіберіп қойған бала қолын аямайды" дегендей, сан түрлі ертегілерді құрастырады. Сондықтан Әблязовқа да, басқасына да бас қатырып, көңіл бөлуге уақытым жоқ", – деген Қырғызстан президенті. SUPER.KG-ге берген сұхбатында Садыр Жапаров бұрынғы президент Алмасбек Атамбаевтың билігі кезінде Мұхтар Әблязовта қырғыз төлқұжаты болғанын және оның Қырғызстанға келуіне қарсы болғанын да айтып өткен. Қазақстандық бұрынғы банкир, қуғындағы оппозиционер Мұхтар Әблязов өткен аптаның ағында "Шумкар" қозғалысының YouTube-арнасына сұхбат беріп, өзіне Садыр Жапаров 2020 жылдың қазанында президент міндетін атқарушы болып тұрғанда телефон шалғанын, оған дейін Түркияда жүргенде де хат жазғанын айтқан. Мәскеудің Таган аудандық соты қазақстандық оппозиционер, БТА Банктің бұрынғы басшысы Мұхтар Әблязовты 2020 жылдың желтоқсанында сырттай 15 жылға бостандығынан айырған. Әблзязов 60 миллиард рубльді (800 миллион доллар) жымқырғаны үшін кінәлі деп танылған. Қазақстанда экс-банкир осыған ұқсас айыппен 2017 жылы 20 жылға, бір жылдан кейін "адам өлтіруге тапсырыс берген" деген айыппен сырттай өмір бойына бостандығынан айырған. 2009 жылдан бері шетелде тұрып жатқан Мұхтар Әблязов Қазақстан билігінің ымырасыз сыншысы ретінде танымал. Ол өзіне тағылған айыптарды жоққа шығарып, олардың саяси астары барын айтып келеді. Мұхтар Әблязов негізін қалаған "Қазақстанның демократиялық таңдауы" қозғалысын 2018 жылы Қазақстан соты "экстремистік" деп танып, тыйым салған . Еуропа парламенті қозғалысты "бейбіт оппозиция" деп атаған. Президент Садыр Жапаровтың билігіне оппозициядағы "Шумкар" атты қозғалысты "Құмтөр голд компани" кәсіпорнының бұрынғы уақытша сыртқы басқарушысы, шетелде жүрген Теңіз Бөлтүрік пен белсенді Самат Күшбекпен бірге құрғанын 12 қазанда шетелден ұсталып әкелінген Сырғақ Кенжебаев жариялады. Олар әлеуметтік желілерде биліктің әрекеттерін сынайтын видеолар жариялап келген. Биыл 12 қазанда Бішкектің Октябрь аудандық соты "Шумкар" қозғалысы мен оның мүшелерінің қызметін экстремистік деп таныды. Сот шешіміне сәйкес, Бөлтүрік, Кенжебаев, Самат Күшбек және Айдар Раевтың қызметі Қырғызстанда террористік және экстремистік деп есептеледі. Президент Садыр Жапаров 12 қазанда Баткен облысының тұрғындарымен кездесуінде оппозициялық "Шумкар" қозғалысы жайлы айта келе, оның мүшелерін "ауру адамдар" деп атаған. 2025 жылы Октябрь аудандық соты Temirov Live, Kloop.kg және "Айт айт десе" медиажобаларының ақпараттық материалдарын, зерттеуші журналист Болот Теміров пен "Клооп" медиасының жетекшісі Ринат Тұхватшиннің қызметін де экстремистік деп тапқан. ОҚИ ОТЫРЫҢЫЗ Қырғыз президенті Садыр Жапаров қызметінде отырып сайлауға қатыса алады деді ОСК басшысы Журналист-зерттеуші Болот Теміров Лондонда халықаралық The Albies сыйлығын алды Тәтішевтің өлімі бойынша сотталған Мұратхан Тоқмәди өтініш түсірді Қазақстан ұйымдарды экстремистік деп тану туралы істерді қарау мерзімін қысқартқысы келеді Журналисті экстремистке теңестірген заман. https://www.hronikatm.com/2026/10/turkme.body: Лента Туркменистан примет участие во встрече «C5+1» Редакция 18 октября 2026 360 Фото: mfa.gov.tm Важное Лента Редакция - 16 октября 2026 Президент Туркменистана прибыл в Армению Лента Редакция - 16 октября 2026 Массовое ДТП в Нижнем устроил уроженец Туркменистана Лента Редакция - 15 октября 2026 Президент Туркменистана прибыл с визитом в Азербайджан Лента Редакция - 15 октября 2026 Аркадаг проиграл Аль-Джазире 19 октября в Самарканде пройдет очередная министерская встреча в формате «C5+1» с участием представителей стран Центральной Азии и США. Подготовку Туркменистана к мероприятию 17 октября на заседании Кабинета Министров представил министр иностранных дел Р. Мередов, сообщает информагентство TDH . На встрече участники обсудят сотрудничество в области цифровизации, образования, здравоохранения, добычи ключевых минералов, энергетики, транспортной инфраструктуры, сельского хозяйства, текстильного производства, финансовое взаимодействие и привлечение инвестиций. Предусмотрена встреча с Мередова с Государственным секретарем США Марко Рубио. В ходе переговоров предполагается рассмотреть возможности расширения двусторонних связей в сферах, представляющих взаимный интерес, а также организационные вопросы предстоящих туркмено-американских политических консультаций. Они запланированы на 3 ноября в Ашхабаде. Бұл туралы 19 қазанда Freedom for Eurasia (FFE) құқық қорғау ұйымы хабарлады. Ұйым деректері бойынша, Бобоев Тәжікстанның қылмыстық кодексінің үш бабы бойынша, оның ішінде "Конституциялық құрылысты күшпен өзгертуге жария түрде шақыру" бабы бойынша кінәлі деп танылған. Қалған айыптар, үкім қашан шыққаны және соттың атауы әзірге жарияланған жоқ. Асадулло Бобоев Еуропада орналасқан "Тәжікстанның реформалары мен дамуы" оппозициялық қозғалысының мүшесі, ол әлеуметтік желілерде Тәжікстан үкіметін сынап келген. 2017 жылы ол отбасымен бірге Тәжікстаннан алдымен Литваға, кейін Германияға кетіп, ол жерден саяси баспана сұраған. 2026 жылғы 8 маусымда Бобоев пен оның 19 жастағы ұлы Мұхаммад Солтүстік Рейн-Вестфалия федералдық жеріндегі миграциялық изоляторға қамалды. Қамауда болған кезінде Бобоев Азаттық радиосына Тәжікстан билігі өзіне қарсы экстремизм бойынша іс қозғағанын айтқан. Германия соты оған отанында қудалауға ұшырау қаупі барын растайтын дәлелдер ұсыну үшін 1 шілдеге дейін мерзім берген. Алайда адвокат ұсынған ондаған бет құжаттарға қарамастан, 20 маусым күні әкелі-балалы екеуін Мюнхеннен Душанбеге жөнелткен. Депортация алдында алдын ала қамау туралы шешімді Гелдерн қаласының соты шығарған. Ондай шешім қабылдауға Бобоевтың Германияда тұруына мүмкіндік беретін ықтиярхат мерзімінің біткені және Германиядан өз еркімен кетуден бас тартқаны негіз болған. FFE бағалауынша, тәжік билігіне саяси қарсылас болған адамның ісі шын мәнінде тек көші-қон заңын бұзу ісі деп қаралған, ал отанына оралғаннан кейін қудалауға ұшырау қаупі тиісті деңгейде бағаланбаған. Душанбеге жеткен бойда Бобоев ұсталып, Тәжікстанның ұлттық қауіпсіздік мемлекеттік комитетінің тергеу изоляторына қамалған. Екі айдан астам уақыт бойы отбасы онымен көрісе алмаған, ал тамақ пен киім-кешек сәлемдемелері қабылданбаған. Оған сондай-ақ тәуелсіз адвокаттың көмегіне жүгінуге рұқсат етпеген. Құқық қорғаушылар Бобоев Тәжікстанға ұшқан кезінде қатыгездікке ұшыраған болуы мүмкін деп хабарлаған. Үкім шыққанға дейін құқық қорғау ұйымдары Германия билігі мен халықаралық құрылымдарды Бобоевтың ісіне араласуға үндеген. 14 шілдеде Польшада орналасқан Тәжікстанның кепілге алынғандар мен саяси тұтқындарды құтқару жөніндегі азаматтық комитеті Германия билігіне, Еуроодаққа, БҰҰ құрылымдарына және Халықаралық Қызыл Крест комитетіне жүгінді. Комитет Бобоевқа тәуелсіз адвокатпен және отбасымен байланысуға мүмкіндік беруді, оның ұсталу жағдайына халықаралық мониторинг жүргізуге рұқсат беруді және оны азаптаудан қорғауды талап етті. 7 шілдеде Human Rights Watch ұйымы да Германияны депортациялау мән-жайларын тексеруге және белсендінің ұсталуына байланысты Душанбеге қысым көрсетуге шақырды. FFE мәлімдемесінде Германия билігінің бұл үндеулерге байланысты ресми жауабы келтірілмеген. FFE деректері бойынша, Асадулло Бобоев 2023 жылдан бері Германия еліне депортациялаған және отанына оралған бойда ұсталғаны белгілі төртінші тәжік оппозициялық белсендісі болып отыр. Бұған дейін Абдулло Шамсиддин, Билол Құрбоналиев және Дилмұрод Эргашев Тәжікстанда тиісінше жеті, он және сегіз жылға бостандығынан айырылған еді. Human Rights Watch оларға қолдан жасалған айыптар тағылған деп есептейді. Австриядан депортацияланған Хизбулло Шовализода Тәжікстанда 20 жылға сотталған. FFE бағалауынша, Бобоевқа кесілген жаза – осы оқиғалардың ішіндегі ең қатаңдарының бірі. "Асадулло Бобоевқа шығарылған үкім – Германияның адамды түрме мен азаптау күтіп тұрған елге жіберу туралы шешімінің тікелей салдары. Диктатураны сынау туралы сөз болғанда, еуропалық мемлекеттер ықтиярхат мәселелерін желеу ете алмайды. Мұндай әрбір депортация – Рахмон режиміне жасалған тарту және барлық тәжік эмигранттарына "Еуропа сіздерді қорғамайды" деген белгі", – деп мәлімдеді FFE төрайымы Лейла Назгүл Сейітбек.
