https://english.news.cn/20261019/08d805e.body: Interview: China's global initiatives reflect shared aspirations of peoples worldwide -- Kyrgyz expert-Xinhua Interview: China's global initiatives reflect shared aspirations of peoples worldwide -- Kyrgyz expert Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-10-19 16:08:45 BISHKEK, Oct. 19 (Xinhua) -- The four major global initiatives proposed by China represent a new philosophical and conceptual approach to human development, and reflect the shared hopes and aspirations of peoples around the world, a Kyrgyz expert said. In a recent interview with Xinhua, Sheradil Baktygulov, a political scientist and director of the Kyrgyz Institute of World Politics, said that the Global Development Initiative, the Global Security Initiative, the Global Civilization Initiative and the Global Governance Initiative complement and reinforce one another. "They reflect key aspects of the activities of various countries and international organizations, regardless of their economic capacity or size, and embody the hopes and aspirations of the world's peoples for the creation of a just and secure society and a community of shared prosperity," he said. In Baktygulov's view, the principles underpinning the four initiatives have been applied in China, producing positive results. "We see that it is precisely on this foundation that China has achieved the heights that have led the entire world to speak of the 'Chinese development miracle'," he said. The expert noted that people around the world are closely examining the foundations of these initiatives, which he believes have served as catalysts for China's economic and technological advancement. "These initiatives have introduced a new philosophical and conceptual approach to human development. In this sense, they can be regarded as an asset that China generously shares with the entire world," he emphasized. This year marks the fifth anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI). According to Baktygulov, this initiative has essentially become a roadmap for achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) on a global scale. "This initiative has enriched humanity's understanding of development and garnered international recognition regarding the pathways and principles required to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals," he said. The political scientist particularly highlighted the GDI's significance for global digital development. "The 'Digital South' initiative under the GDI reflects a new digital reality that advocates for the creation of operational standards and rules to bridge the digital divide and prevent digital inequality," Baktygulov said. That plays a vital role in aligning the trends of this new reality with the needs of countries in the Global South and is therefore welcomed by them, he added. ■ Interview: China's global initiatives reflect shared aspirations of peoples worldwide -- Kyrgyz expert

https://www.vedomosti.ru/politics/articl.body: US Department of State / Flickr Госсекретарь США Марко Рубио 17 октября прибыл в узбекистанский Самарканд на трехдневный министерский саммит формата С5+1 (пять государств Центральной Азии + Вашингтон). Представитель госдепартамента 16 октября заявил, что «слишком долго Соединенные Штаты сосредотачивались на Ближнем Востоке и Востоке, и этот регион, Центральная Азия, не получал того внимания, которого заслуживает». Сам же Рубио на своей странице в Х (экс-Twitter) подчеркнул, что направляется в это турне, включающее визит в Индию, чтобы продолжить укрепление экономических возможностей США при администрации президента Дональда Трампа . Президент США пригласил президентов Казахстана и Узбекистана Касым-Жомарта Токаева и Шавката Мирзиёева на саммит G20 во Флориде в декабре 2026 г. В этом году упор саммита С5+1 сделан на бизнес – с Рубио отправились 200 представителей американского бизнеса, а госдеп особо подчеркнул, что госсекретарь «возглавляет делегацию» бизнесменов. В бизнес-делегацию в Самарканд, по данным американских СМИ, вошли представители Boeing, Citibank и инвестфонда Franklin Templeton, а также компаний, занимающихся добычей критических минералов. 15 октября спецпосланник президента США по Центральной и Южной Азии Серджио Гор (настоящее имя Сергей Гороховский, уроженец Ташкента) заявил, что в Центральной Азии «есть одни из самых богатых месторождений и они ищут надежных, заслуживающих доверия партнеров; и мы считаем, что американские компании могут предложить такие решения». Главное из выступления Путина на саммите СНГ Политика Значение Центральной Азии возросло благодаря положению в центре Евразии, минеральным ресурсам, демографическим и экономическим показателям, говорит доцент кафедры международного бизнеса Финансового университета при правительстве России Артем Пылин. Стратегия США в регионе – при формальном содействии укреплению суверенитета стран региона, развитию инвестиционного сотрудничества, региональной связности и безопасности – расширять экономическое присутствие, говорит Пылин. По отчету американского Центра инициатив по лидерству в Азии (CALI), в 2025 г. на долю США приходилось 19% прямых иностранных инвестиций в регионе – $51 млрд. По более скромным последним доступным официальным данным госдепартамента от 2020 г., с начала 1990-х гг. американские инвестиции составляли $31 млрд, не считая финансовой поддержки от правительства на сумму около $9,2 млрд. Как сообщалось на инвестфоруме в Бишкеке в 2024 г., 99% американских инвестиций пришлись на Казахстан, в основном в нефтедобычу. Chevron и ExxonMobil добывают до трети казахстанской нефти, что сопоставимо с добычей госкомпании «КазМунайГаз». Эти же компании входят вместе с российской «Транснефтью» и другими в Каспийский трубопроводный консорциум , который управляет нефтепроводом до Новороссийска. Из последних крупных американских контрактов – рекордная для региона сделка 2025 г. Wabtec о поставке 300 локомотивов для казахстанской железной дороги, часть которых изготовят в Астане. В ноябре 2025 г. подписано соглашение о привлечении $1,6 млрд на 10 лет при координации Citibank и гарантиях Экспортно-импортного банка США (EXIM) для развития «Срединного маршрута» из Центральной Азии через Каспий и Кавказ в Европу. Тогда же Cove Capital получила 70% в вольфрамовых проектах Карагандинской области, способных дать 15% мировых поставок этого критически важного металла преимущественно на американский рынок, снижая зависимость США от Китая. Реализация проекта оценивается в $1,1 млрд за три года, $900 млн готов дать EXIM. Пока что американские инвестиции в регион сосредоточены в сырьевом секторе, в основном в ТЭК Казахстана. По словам Пылина, в рамках курса администрации Дональда Трампа наблюдается смещение интереса к критическим минералам с упором на Казахстан и Узбекистан. Центральная Азия остается хабом для поставок американских товаров и на российский рынок – там есть сборочные и пищевые производства, говорит он. Читайте также: Россия и Киргизия утвердили план военного сотрудничества на 2027 год Для сравнения: объем российских инвестиций в Центральной Азии, согласно заявлению президента России Владимира Путина на региональном саммите в Душанбе в декабре 2025 г., составляет $20 млрд. Китайские, по подсчетам Евразийского банка развития, – $36 млрд. В торговле с Центральной Азией Китай лидер с 2024 г. В 2025 г. товарооборот Китая и стран региона, по данным минкоммерции КНР, составил $106,3 млрд. На втором месте Россия с $50 млрд, у США в 2025 г. товарооборот со странами Центральной Азии составил менее $10 млрд. США, исключая проекты ТЭКа, инвестируют в регион в сравнении с другими направлениями ограниченные средства, отмечает завсектором Центральной Азии ИМЭМО РАН Станислав Притчин. Американскому бизнесу, кроме добычи природных ресурсов, Центральная Азия малоинтересна, считает эксперт. «Много вопросов в логистике, инвестиционном режиме, хотя власти работают над его улучшением. Реализация анонсированных проектов, инвестиций и закупок не выведет США в сопоставимые с Китаем партнеры региона», – отметил он. Конкурировать США с граничащими с регионом Китаем и Россией сложно, на преодоление логистической удаленности направлены Срединный коридор и «Маршрут Трампа», говорит Пылин: «Необходимы инвестиции, которых пока мало с учетом потенциала окупаемости». Американцы пытаются застолбить роль оператора вывода центральноазиатских компаний на международные IPO, подключить к площадкам, финансовым центрам, которые в Казахстане уже есть, а аналогичные планируется открыть в Узбекистане, говорит Притчин: «Но это точечные проекты, скорее, сервисное обслуживание, а не реальные инвестиции». Соответствующий проект указа президента вынесен на общественное обсуждение . Согласно справке-обоснованию, изменения направлены на ускорение рассмотрения ходатайств и устранение проблем, возникающих при организации заседаний комиссий. В частности, предлагается сократить состав Комиссии по вопросам помилования с девяти до не менее чем семи человек. Сейчас заседание считается правомочным, если в нем участвуют не менее двух третей от общего числа членов. По данным разработчиков проекта, обеспечить необходимый кворум на практике бывает сложно, из-за чего рассмотрение ходатайств затягивается. Суд оставил приговор в силе Кроме того, предлагается исключить протокол заседания наблюдательной комиссии при местных государственных администрациях и органах местного самоуправления из перечня обязательных документов, прилагаемых к материалам о помиловании. Сейчас такие комиссии должны рассматривать поступившие материалы в течение десяти рабочих дней и оформлять заключение, которое носит рекомендательный характер. При этом сложности с обеспечением кворума также могут задерживать подготовку документов. Читайте также: Ребенок и сексуализированное насилие. Что важно знать родителям Проект предусматривает возможность повторного обращения за помилованием для людей, которых уже помиловали ранее. В справке-обосновании отмечается, что действующее законодательство прямо не запрещает подавать такие ходатайства, однако отдельный механизм их рассмотрения не установлен. Новая норма должна устранить этот пробел. Также разработчики предлагают уточнить случаи и сроки подачи повторных ходатайств осужденными, а также конкретизировать критерии "трудной жизненной ситуации", которая может учитываться при повторном обращении. В качестве обстоятельств, заслуживающих внимания, в документе упоминается тяжелая жизненная ситуация семьи осужденного или его близких родственников, нуждающихся в его помощи. Такие обстоятельства должны подтверждаться документами уполномоченных органов. По мнению разработчиков, более четкое определение критериев позволит избежать разночтений и произвольного толкования нормы. Проектом предлагается утвердить новое Положение о порядке осуществления помилования в Кыргызстане и признать утратившим силу указ президента от 14 июня 2024 года No157. Суд оставил приговор в силе Общество 976 19 октября 2026 10:56 Kaktus Все самое интересное в Telegram В Бишкеке суд оставил в силе приговор мужчине, осужденному на девять лет лишения свободы за убийство знакомого. Тот утверждал, что не собирался убивать потерпевшего, а ранил его случайно во время драки. Однако кассационная инстанция не нашла оснований для пересмотра дела. Постановление Верховного суда размещено на портале "Цифровое правосудие". Имена изменены. Согласно материалам дела, преступление произошло утром 7 ноября 2024 года в квартире осужденного Андрея. Мужчина находился в состоянии алкогольного опьянения, когда между ним и его знакомым произошла словесная перепалка. Во время конфликта Андрей ударил знакомого ножом в грудь. Потерпевший скончался на месте до приезда скорой помощи. Читайте также: В ООН призвали готовиться к изменениям из-за ИИ. Кто рискует остаться позади? Из материалов дела следует, что Андрей познакомился с потерпевшим в сентябре 2024 года. После совместного распития спиртного он предложил знакомому пожить у него и работать вместе, поскольку тому негде было жить. Впоследствии мужчины проживали вместе, работали и употребляли алкоголь. По словам осужденного, накануне происшествия они снова выпивали, после чего знакомый ушел из квартиры. Потерпевший, как указал Андрей, употреблял синтетический наркотик, несмотря на его запреты. Позвонив ему, осужденный решил, что тот продолжает употреблять спиртное и, возможно, наркотики. Тогда он потребовал, чтобы знакомый забрал свои вещи и съехал. Утром 7 ноября потерпевший пришел к осужденному вместе с несколькими знакомыми, чтобы забрать личные вещи. Как рассказали свидетели, перед этим они пили водку. В суде Андрей заявил, что между ним и пришедшими мужчинами началась потасовка. По его версии, один из них стал наносить ему удары и он схватил нож, чтобы защититься. Осужденный утверждал, что намеревался ударить нападавшего, но случайно попал в другого мужчину, умысла на убийство у него не было. Однако показания свидетелей отличались от версии Андрея. Одна из свидетельниц рассказала, что во время конфликта осужденный толкнул ее в сторону шкафа, из-за чего она упала вместе с мебелью. Когда женщина стала подниматься, она увидела, как Андрей с ножом направился в сторону одного из мужчин. Однако, замахнувшись, он ударил ножом другого участника конфликта - в область груди. Другой свидетель сообщил, что пытался защищаться от Андрея с помощью сковородки. По его словам, после удара ножом потерпевший некоторое время оставался на ногах, затем упал и начал хрипеть. Присутствовавшие вызвали скорую помощь и милицию. Еще один свидетель признал, что ударил Андрея кулаком после того, как тот толкнул женщину. По его словам, затем тот достал нож и попытался ударить его, но промахнулся. После этого он целенаправленно ударил ножом потерпевшего, который стоял рядом. Читайте также: Могут быть галлюцинации. Врач предупредил, что энергетики не заменяют отдых и сон Согласно заключению судебно-медицинской экспертизы, смерть мужчины наступила в результате проникающего колото-резаного ранения грудной клетки с повреждением правого легкого и внутренним кровотечением. В правой плевральной полости обнаружили около 1,3 литра крови со сгустками. Эксперты установили, что глубина раневого канала составляла около 15 сантиметров. Повреждение было квалифицировано как тяжкий вред здоровью по признаку опасности для жизни. Судебно-психиатрическая экспертиза показала, что Андрей не страдает психическим заболеванием. На момент происшествия он находился в состоянии обычного алкогольного опьянения, мог осознавать свои действия и руководить ими. Его признали вменяемым. Кроме того, в материалах дела имелась видеозапись продолжительностью 56 секунд, сделанная одним из свидетелей после происшествия. На ней осужденный держал в руках нож, похожий на тот, который изъяли при осмотре места происшествия. Экспертиза установила, что изъятый нож являлся хозяйственно-бытовым предметом и не относился к холодному оружию. Суд также исследовал показания свидетелей, результаты биологических и криминалистических экспертиз, протоколы осмотра места происшествия и другие материалы уголовного дела. Ленинский районный суд Бишкека признал Андрея виновным в убийстве по части 1 статьи 122 Уголовного кодекса КР и назначил ему девять лет лишения свободы с отбыванием наказания в колонии строгого режима. Бишкекский городской суд оставил приговор без изменений, а апелляционную жалобу - без удовлетворения. Осужденный обратился с кассационной жалобой, в которой просил объективно рассмотреть дело и утверждал, что ответственность за смерть потерпевшего лежит на других людях. Кассационная судебная коллегия изучила материалы дела, показания участников конфликта и заключения экспертиз. Судьи пришли к выводу, что доказательства были исследованы полно и получили надлежащую оценку, а выводы судов первой и апелляционной инстанций являются обоснованными. В итоге приговор Ленинского районного суда и решение Бишкекского городского суда оставлены в силе. Кассационную жалобу осужденного отклонили. https://www.gazeta.uz/en/2026/10/19/law/.body: Photo: Eldos Fazylbekov / Gazeta Uzbekistan toughens penalties for sexual violence against children President Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a law toughening penalties for sexual violence against children under 14, including life imprisonment. The statute of limitations for rape of minors has been abolished. Fines for sexual harassment have also been increased. Ўзбек тилида O‘zbek tilida На русском языке Today, 11:57 Politics President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev signed a law toughening penalties for all forms of violence against children. The document was adopted by the Legislative Chamber of the Oliy Majlis on 30 September and approved by the Senate on 2 October. The amendments entered into force on 14 October. One of the key changes is that those who commit sexual violence against children under 14 may now face life imprisonment, while the statute of limitations for rape of persons under 18 has been abolished. Sentences for intentional crimes resulting in a child’s death cannot be reduced. Fines for sexual harassment have also been increased. Presidential Administration head Saida Mirziyoyeva, commenting on the signing of the law, said : “Everyone who causes harm and pain to a child will be held accountable, from employees of educational institutions to family members who commit violence.” “A child’s safety cannot depend on circumstances. Anyone who infringes children’s lives, health and dignity must know that they will not escape severe punishment,” she stressed. Up to life imprisonment for rape of minors: amendments to the Criminal Code Rape of a person under 14 is now punishable by 15 to 25 years in prison or life imprisonment, compared with 15 to 20 years previously (article 118, part 4 of the code). The same penalties apply to the violent gratification of sexual desire in an unnatural form involving a person under 14, where violence, threats or the victim’s helpless condition are involved. Previously, the penalty was also 15 to 20 years in prison (article 119, part 4). When sentencing offenders convicted of these offenses, courts may no longer take into account mitigating circumstances, such as voluntary surrender, sincere remorse, active assistance in solving the crime or voluntary compensation for the harm caused (article 57−1). Courts may no longer exempt offenders from criminal liability because the statute of limitations has expired in cases involving these crimes, as well as rape of a person under 18 (article 118, part 3, clause “a”) and the violent satisfaction of sexual desire in an unnatural form involving a person under 18 (article 119, part 3, clause “a”) (article 64). Those convicted of these crimes (article 118, part 3, clause “a” and part 4; article 119, part 3, clause “a” and part 4) may no longer be released from serving their sentences on the grounds that the limitation period for sentence enforcement has expired (article 69). Suspended sentences (article 72) and parole (article 73) may no longer be granted for intentional crimes that result in a child’s death. The rule limiting prison terms to two-thirds of the maximum sentence prescribed in the Special Part of the Criminal Code no longer applies to women and men over 60 convicted of these offenses (article 50). Indecent acts committed without violence against a person under 16 by a group are now punishable by restriction of liberty for 3 to 5 years or imprisonment for 3 to 5 years (article 129, amended to include offenses committed by a group). Tougher penalties for sexual harassment: changes in Administrative Liability Code Sexual harassment (article 41−1 of the code) is now punishable by a fine of 10 to 15 basic calculation units or administrative detention for up to 10 days. Previously, the penalty was a fine of 2 to 5 basic calculation units or detention for up to 5 days. Advertising on Gazeta The same offense, if repeated within one year of the imposition of an administrative penalty, is punishable by a fine of 15 to 20 basic calculation units or detention for up to 15 days. Previously, the fine ranged from 5 to 7 basic calculation units, while the maximum detention period was 15 days. https://kz.kursiv.media/en/2026-10-19/en.body: Illustration by Kursiv.media, photo editor: Adelina Mamedova The number of registered media outlets in Kazakhstan has grown from 2,900 to more than 5,400 over the past decade, while nearly 40% of the population now gets news through social media and messaging apps. Kanat Iskakov , first vice minister of culture and information, shared the figures during a panel discussion at Astana Media Week , held on Oct. 14-16. How news consumption has changed According to Iskakov, 10 years ago, 73% of Kazakhstan’s population used the internet, while television was the primary source of news. Today, internet access has reached 93.4%. News consumption habits have also changed. Some 39.1% of Kazakhstanis now get news through social media and messaging apps — a larger share than those who rely primarily on news websites or television, according to the figures presented at the forum. Read also: Code, power, and exile: The untold story of Pavel Durov and Telegram . Pavel Durov, cover design by Victor Melamed / Collage by Kursiv.media, photo editor: Dastan Shanay Bloggers compete with newsrooms Iskakov said Telegram channels had evolved into full-fledged media outlets, while bloggers and influencers increasingly competed with traditional newsrooms. In some cases, they also set the news agenda and shape public opinion. «In just 10 years, we have transitioned from a traditional media system to a multichannel digital environment. Today, newsrooms, bloggers and digital platforms are all vying for the audience’s attention,» Iskakov said. More people turn to AI chatbots for news Artificial intelligence is driving another phase of change in the media landscape, Iskakov said. Readers are increasingly turning to chatbots to find news, get summaries of events and seek explanations of current affairs. He cited international research indicating that the share of people worldwide who use AI chatbots for news at least once a week rose from 7% to 10% over the past year. Read also: Clicks vs. cash: What readers really value in their news . Image generated by neural network, photo editor: Adelina Mamedova Media formats are converging Speaking on the sidelines of the forum, Iskakov said the boundaries between traditional media formats were becoming less distinct. Television, online publications and newspapers, once operating through separate channels, are increasingly converging within a unified digital environment. Television networks are developing streaming services, while online outlets are expanding into video, producing segments and interviews for digital audiences. «Previously, changes took years or even decades; now, they happen every single day,» Iskakov said. The first Astana Media Week was held in October 2017. The 2026 event marked the forum’s 10th edition. Astana Media Week 2026 / Photo: Kursiv.media Notably, the vice minister has also called for clearer labeling of content created with artificial intelligence, saying audiences should be informed when AI has been used to produce material. https://english.news.cn/20261018/83286f7.body: World Insights: LatAm journalists explore drivers of China's NEV industry-Xinhua World Insights: LatAm journalists explore drivers of China's NEV industry Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-10-18 22:58:15 A journalist from Peru test-drives a new energy vehicle at Li Auto's manufacturing base in Changzhou, east China's Jiangsu Province, Oct. 14, 2026. (Photo by Zhao Yanchao/Xinhua) by Xinhua writers He Yixuan, Xi Yue, Zhao Yanchao CHANGZHOU, China, Oct. 18 (Xinhua) -- Cameras clicking and smartphones raised, a group of Latin American journalists moved through the production workshops of a Chinese new energy vehicle (NEV) maker in Changzhou, east China's Jiangsu Province, capturing robots at work and vehicles taking shape on the assembly line. For some, the scene offered a glimpse into the technology behind Chinese electric vehicles (EVs) they had already seen on the streets back home. Thousands of kilometers away, Chinese-made EVs are becoming part of everyday life in Latin America, while charging facilities and power transmission projects are opening up new avenues for green cooperation. During the 2026 Belt and Road Journalists Forum, dozens of journalists from Latin American countries visited Changzhou, known as China's "capital of new energy," to explore the industrial strengths behind China's green development and discover opportunities for cooperation with Latin America. FROM FACTORY FLOORS TO EVERYDAY MOBILITY For Rody Olivera, president of the Uruguayan Press Association, the visit was more than a tour of a manufacturing facility. Having purchased a Chinese NEV in May, he was eager to see how it was made. Inside the welding workshop at Li Auto's manufacturing base in Changzhou, he said the visit had confirmed that he had "made the right decision." "The factory is impressive in terms of its size and productivity. Electric vehicles offer many advantages, as they provide a quieter driving experience, numerous driver-assistance features and greater comfort," Olivera said. In his view, China's progress in the sector stems from both policy support and industrial capabilities. "China is a pioneer in this technology," he said, attributing the country's achievements to its innovation capabilities and the development of a complete industrial chain. A journalist from Mexico test-rides an electric scooter in Segway-Ninebot, a renowned electric two-wheeler maker, in Changzhou, east China's Jiangsu Province, Oct. 13, 2026. (Photo by Zhao Yanchao/Xinhua) At the exhibition hall of Segway-Ninebot, a renowned electric two-wheeler maker, Angel Sanchez, president of the Federation of Journalists of Peru, recognized the company's electric scooters, saying they could offer a convenient transportation option for young people and office workers in Peru. "They have many advantages, including quick responsiveness, flexible center-of-gravity control and a portable design," Sanchez said, adding that China's development of new energy and other emerging technologies ultimately aims to improve people's lives. Such products offer a glimpse into the broader industrial ecosystem that has taken shape in Changzhou. Its industrial chain spans five areas: energy generation, storage, transmission, consumption and distribution networks. In 2025, the scale of the city's new energy industry exceeded 1 trillion yuan (about 150 billion U.S. dollars). CONNECTING INDUSTRIAL STRENGTHS WITH LOCAL NEEDS The city's industrial strengths extend from NEVs and key components to charging infrastructure and power transmission equipment, creating opportunities for cooperation across different stages of the energy transition. At the exhibition area of charging infrastructure operator Star Charge, Virgilio Arias, president of Mexico's Front Page Club, stopped in front of a photograph showing an electric-bus charging station in Mexico City. Journalists visit Star Charge, a charging infrastructure operator, in Changzhou, east China's Jiangsu Province, Oct. 14, 2026. (Photo by Zhao Yanchao/Xinhua) "I've just learned that this Chinese company has provided charging facilities for three Bus Rapid Transit lines in Mexico City and Monterrey, supporting the operation of more than 150 electric buses," Arias said. The example highlighted how Chinese technologies are being applied to local transportation systems in Latin America. As Mexico and other countries in the region accelerate their energy transitions, cooperation in charging infrastructure and electric mobility could help address practical needs while advancing shared sustainable development goals, Arias said. Green cooperation also extends beyond transportation to the infrastructure needed to transmit clean energy over long distances. For Samira de Castro, president of the National Federation of Journalists of Brazil, a visit to NR Electric brought an unexpected connection to a project she had covered years earlier. In 2012, she wrote a report on Brazil's Belo Monte hydropower project. During her visit in Changzhou, she learned that the company's technology had been used in the project's second-phase ultra-high-voltage transmission system. Now operational, the transmission project helps deliver hydropower from northern Brazil to distant consumption centers, including areas serving Rio de Janeiro. Castro said the advanced technology had made a significant contribution to Brazil's electricity supply and changed the lives of local residents. TURNING SHARED GOALS INTO GREEN COOPERATION "There is an ecosystem of companies here that are collaborating to advance clean energy. Renewable energy is the future, and it is happening right here, right now," said Geraldo Cantarino, a member of the Brazilian Press Association, during his first visit to China. For Latin American countries with diverse energy resources and growing demand for cleaner development, cooperation with China could create further opportunities in equipment manufacturing, infrastructure construction and the application of new energy technologies. For the journalists visiting Changzhou, the trip offered a closer look at the industrial capabilities underpinning China's new energy development and their potential relevance to Latin America. From EVs and smart mobility products to charging networks and power transmission systems, the examples they encountered demonstrated how green cooperation can take shape across an interconnected industrial chain. Journalists learn about power transmission technologies while visiting NR Electric in Changzhou, east China's Jiangsu Province, Oct. 14, 2026. (Photo by Zhao Yanchao/Xinhua) As the visit drew to a close, the journalists took away more than photographs of production lines, electric scooters and power transmission equipment. They had also gained a firsthand understanding of how technologies developed in a Chinese industrial hub could connect with the green development ambitions of countries across Latin America. For Castro, the next step was to share these observations with a wider audience. "As a journalist, I hope to tell more people the stories of China-Latin America cooperation in the new energy sector, so that the world can see China's commitment to high-quality development, openness and cooperation," she said. ■ You may like Autumn scenery in Mudanjiang, China's Heilongjiang Desert self-driving event kicks off in Zhongwei, China's Ningxia Parade of intangible cultural heritage dances held in Liaoning In pics: flower decoration themed on 2026 APEC "China Year" in Shenzhen View of blooming flowers in Xiamen, China's Fujian Sea of clouds seen above Yellow River's Hukou Waterfall in China's Shanxi More from GLOBALink Inside China's "unlikely" AI computing hub Trendy China | China's new energy industry through foreign journalists' eyes China's Xinjiang embraces cotton harvest

https://asiaplus.news/en/2026/10/19/seve.body: Share Aleksey Korchagin , asia+ Categories Sport Tajikistan Format News Published 19.10.2026 16:05 Translations Eng Рус Seven champions were crowned at Tajikistan’s President’s Judo Cup in Kulob on October 17–18, with a total prize fund of 1.26 million somoni awarded to medalists across seven men’s weight categories. The tournament brought together established members of the national team and judokas seeking to strengthen their positions in the national rankings. In the 60 kg category, Mehrzod Sufiyev won gold, repeating his success at the tournament in 2023. Nourullo Ahmadov took silver, while Jasour Lutfishoyev and Mustafo Nourov shared bronze. Nourov also won bronze in the same category in 2023. Iskandar Mahmadkhojazoda claimed gold in the 66 kg category, defeating Sarvar Abdushukurov in the final. Abdushukurov recently won bronze in kurash at the 2026 Asian Games in the 66 kg category. Ehson Safarzoda and Mustafoi Abdulfayz took bronze. National team standout Emomali Nourali did not compete in Kulob as he prepares for the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam, scheduled for October 29–31. Mahmadkhojazoda is also entered for the upcoming tournament. Masoud Ahmadzod won the 73 kg category, with Benyomin Nazirov taking silver and Bobojon Sharopov and Umar Sherov earning bronze. The category includes Muhiddin Asadulloyev, a bronze medalist at the 2026 Asian Games who currently ranks second in the International Judo Federation’s world rankings. Four champions crowned on the second day Abubakr Boqiyev won the 81 kg category, having previously claimed the President’s Cup in the 73 kg division in 2023. Bakhtiyor Bozorov took silver, while Muhammadrahim Sarakhonov and Sunatulo Musoyev won bronze. In the 90 kg category, Muzammir Karimzoda claimed gold, followed by Rasoul Umarov with silver. Hamroz Rajabov and Muhammadiqbol Toshev shared bronze. Somoni Kishvarov won the 100 kg category, finishing ahead of silver medalist Sunatulo Mirzoumarzoda. Isroil Rahimov and Firdavs Nasimov took bronze. Asian Games silver medalist Jahongir Majidov, also entered for the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam, was among the leading Tajik judokas in this weight class. Parviz Abdurahmonov won the over-100 kg category. Sharifjon Nazriyev took silver, while Mansour Rahmon and Nekruzshoh Nekbakhtzoda shared bronze. Both bronze medalists are entered for the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam. Rahmon also represented Tajikistan in the heavyweight division at the recent Asian Games in Japan. Prize money and upcoming international competition Across the seven categories, 28 medals were awarded: seven gold, seven silver and 14 bronze. Each champion received 70,000 somoni, silver medalists received 50,000 somoni each, and bronze medalists received 30,000 somoni each, bringing the total prize payout to 1.26 million somoni. The tournament followed shortly after the 2026 Asian Games in Japan, where Tajikistan’s judo team won four medals: silver for Jahongir Majidov and bronze for Muhiddin Asadulloyev, Abubakr Sherov and Ahliya Muminova. The next major challenge for the country’s judokas is the Abu Dhabi Grand Slam in the United Arab Emirates on October 29–31. Tajikistan has entered 16 athletes, including several competitors who took part in the President’s Cup in Kulob. Join us on social media! Today, 13:30 3 min read 2 084 views 0 comments 0 Source: Screenshot U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio addressed questions about the war in Ukraine during a meeting with journalists in Samarkand on October 19, stating that no one would emerge victorious from the conflict. According to Rubio, U.S. President Donald Trump is prepared to support initiatives aimed at ending the war between Russia and Ukraine. "The president has made it clear that he wants the war to end. He wants the war between Ukraine and Russia to come to a conclusion. We will continue to do everything in our power to contribute to resolving the conflict," Rubio said. "No one wins in the war in Ukraine. People are dying every single day. Every day, there are explosions and destruction," he added . Citing Trump, Rubio stated that 25,000 people are losing their lives every month as a result of the war. Rubio also responded to statements made by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy regarding the temporary suspension and subsequent resumption of U.S. intelligence sharing. Zelenskyy had previously discussed the issue in an interview with NBC News. "I don't know where he gets this information or why he is speaking to the press about it. There was no pause in the transmission of intelligence. I repeat: Zelensky should be focusing on ending the war right now. Both we and Russia need to focus on that as well," Rubio said. The Secretary of State also addressed earlier reports suggesting that the United States had failed to warn Ukraine about a missile attack on Kyiv. According to Rubio, a malfunction had occurred in Ukraine's early warning system. "A software issue arose a few days ago. U.S. European Command is looking into the situation," he stated. During the press exchange, a journalist asked Rubio what evidence suggested that Russian President Vladimir Putin was willing to participate in peace negotiations. "What kind of evidence? This isn't a criminal case; it's diplomacy. In diplomacy, you keep moving forward," Rubio responded. He also commented on Trump's decision to delay imposing additional sanctions against Russia. "Trump has paused the sanctions for 60 days because he wants to see if there is a possibility for the ongoing negotiations to succeed," Rubio said. Rubio arrived in Samarkand on October 18, accompanied by more than 200 business representatives, to participate in the C5+1 summit. He was welcomed by Saida Mirziyoyeva, Head of Uzbekistan's Presidential Administration, and Foreign Minister Bakhtiyor Saidov. During his visit, Rubio is scheduled to meet with representatives of the five Central Asian countries before traveling to Mumbai and Jamnagar in India. Explaining the purpose of his visit to Uzbekistan, Rubio said: "You know, typically, one might visit a country because a crisis or problem has arisen there, or to attend a conference. However, there are also countries with which we simply wish to develop our relations. Our trips to Greece and other nations a few weeks ago fall into this category. Just a few weeks prior to this visit, we traveled to Latin America, and now we are visiting Central Asia." # AQSH tashqi siyosati # C5+1 sammiti # Diplomatik muzokaralar # markaziy osiyo # marko rubio # samarqand # ukraina urushi Reporter Xadicha Abdurashidova All stories Telegram channel @daryo_eng Subscribe What do you think? https://kz.kursiv.media/en/2026-10-19/en.body: Kazakhstan’s health ministry assesses risk of mpox spread as low Published October 19, 2026 11:52 Nikolai Marchenko Senior Journalist n.marchenko@kursiv.media Olesya Bassarova General News Correspondent o.bassarova@kursiv.kz Photo: Unsplash, photo editor: Milosh Muratovskiy Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Healthcare considers the risk of a widespread mpox outbreak in the country to be low but does not rule out imported cases. Health screening and quarantine measures have therefore been strengthened at border checkpoints. «Given the reported cases in several countries around the world ... the possibility of the infection being imported into Kazakhstan cannot be ruled out. The risk of widespread mpox transmission among the population is considered low, taking into account the characteristics of pathogen transmission,» the ministry said in a statement. To prevent the infection from being imported and spreading, Kazakhstan has tightened health screening at its borders. Border checkpoints have been equipped with non-contact thermometers, and medical facilities and laboratories are ready to detect the disease. Procedures are also in place to ensure coordination between agencies if a particularly dangerous infectious disease is suspected. These measures are being implemented under a directive issued by Kazakhstan’s Chief State Sanitary Doctor. According to the ministry, health screening across all modes of transport has so far found no travelers suspected of having mpox. Mpox is a viral infection that spreads through close physical contact with an infected person, including contact with rashes and bodily fluids. The virus can also spread through contaminated clothing, bedding and other items, as well as through contact with infected animals. The main symptoms of mpox include fever, headache, muscle aches, swollen lymph nodes and a skin rash. As a preventive measure, the Ministry of Healthcare recommends avoiding close contact with people who have unexplained skin rashes or other signs of infection. If symptoms of mpox appear, especially after travel to countries where cases have been reported, medical advice should be sought and the doctor informed about the trip and any possible contact with infected people. Previous reports said that five people suspected of having mpox had been hospitalized in Russia. Share Link copied

https://en.kabar.kg/news/state-auditing-.body: Kabar Agency Bishkek, Oct. 19, 2026. /Kabar/. The consolidated budget of Kyrgyzstan has surpassed 1 trillion soms, which has increased the responsibility for the use of state funds; therefore, every som of the budget must serve the people. This was stated in a congratulatory message from President Sadyr Zhaparov to the participants of an event marking the 30th anniversary of the establishment of the Chamber of Accounts. The head of state noted that the history of the Chamber of Accounts is closely linked to the country’s development path throughout its years of independence, and emphasized that the Constitutional Law adopted on May 31, 2023, marked the beginning of a new stage in the development of state auditing. "Today, the Chamber of Accounts is an institution that conducts state audits and holds a special place in ensuring state financial discipline," the message says. The president highlighted that, given the expansion of the state budget’s capacity and the implementation of major infrastructure and social projects across the country, the effective use of state funds takes on particular importance. "We must not only verify where budget funds are directed, but also clearly see what results they have delivered for the state and the people. Audit findings should be measured by concrete changes in public administration, and the recommendations provided must be implemented in practice," Sadyr Zhaparov emphasized. He also noted the necessity of maintaining the independence of the Chamber of Accounts, as well as the objectivity and professional integrity of its auditors. According to the head of state, the introduction of digital mechanisms has enhanced the transparency of financial and economic operations and created new opportunities for identifying shadow economic activity. Electronic waybills and electronic invoices help facilitate the work of state audit authorities. "We must reach a new level in the work of state auditing. Activities should be aimed not only at addressing the consequences of offenses that have already occurred but also at developing the capacity to prevent them," the president stated in his congratulatory message. Furthermore, Sadyr Zhaparov noted that the Chamber of Accounts should become an institution that identifies risks in advance and contributes to improving the quality of public administration. He added that cooperation and the exchange of experience with international supreme audit institutions are also important. The president expressed his gratitude to veterans for their contributions to strengthening state financial discipline and developing the country, and he wished the staff of the Chamber of Accounts success in their vital and responsible work. It should be noted that the president’s congratulatory address was read out by Adylbek Kasymaliev, Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. Print

https://24.kg/article/batma-zholboldueva.body: Активистка Батма Жолболдуева отправилась пешком из Баткенской области в Бишкек, добиваясь решения своего вопроса. Несмотря на встречу с представителями областной администрации, она отказалась прекращать путь. Об этом сообщила пресс-служба полномочного представителя президента в Баткенской области. По данным ведомства, 18 октября, после появления информации о пешем походе Жолболдуевой, полпред президента Мамыржан Рахимов поручил разобраться в ситуации, разъяснить активистке законные способы решения ее проблемы и принять во внимание ее безопасность. Первый заместитель полпреда Бактыбек Токсонбаев встретился с Жолболдуевой в селе Жаны-Жер Баткенского района. Во время разговора ей объяснили порядок рассмотрения обращения, однако она не согласилась с предложенным вариантом и продолжила путь в Бишкек. В областной администрации также сообщили, что ведут переговоры с администрацией президента об организации личного приема Батмы Жолболдуевой у Садыра Жапарова. По информации администрации президента, сейчас утверждается план мероприятий по проведению встречи главы государства с жителями Баткенской области. После согласования списка граждан, которые смогут попасть на личный прием, предполагается организовать встречу с участием представителей профильных министерств. При этом в официальном сообщении не уточняется, чего именно добивается Батма Жолболдуева. Областная администрация заявила о готовности рассматривать обращения граждан и содействовать решению их проблем в рамках законодательства. Напомним, в декабре 2024 года блогер Батмакан Жолболдуева заявила об изнасиловании ее в ИВС, бездействии правоохранительных, надзорных органов и чиновников. https://www.trend.az/azerbaijan/4236435..body: Home Azerbaijan TABIB placed under Azerbaijan's Ministry of Health - decree Azerbaijan News 19 October 2026 11:27 (UTC +04:00) Photo: Artificial intelligence Aysel Mammadli Editor Read more BAKU, Azerbaijan, October 19. The public legal entity Management Union of Medical Territorial Units (TABIB) has been placed under the authority of Azerbaijan's Ministry of Health. President Ilham Aliyev has signed a decree to this effect. The document was published on the official website of the President of Azerbaijan. Under the decree, the rights, obligations and property of the existing public legal entity will be transferred to TABIB, which will operate under the Ministry of Health. TABIB's authorized capital will be formed from the property of the existing public legal entity. Until TABIB is registered in accordance with the Law of the Republic of Azerbaijan on State Registration and the State Register of Legal Entities, the existing public legal entity will continue operating. During this period, the powers of its Supervisory Board will be exercised by a commission established by the Ministry of Health. TABIB's day-to-day management will be carried out by a Management Board consisting of a chairperson and four deputy chairpersons, all appointed and dismissed by the Ministry of Health. The decree assigns the following founder's powers over TABIB to the President of Azerbaijan: - Approval of TABIB's charter and determination of the amount of its authorized capital, as well as amendments to them; - Establishment of TABIB's governing bodies; - Reorganization and liquidation of TABIB; - Adoption of the decision stipulated in Article 3.3 of the Law on Public Legal Entities. The Ministry of Health is entrusted with resolving other matters falling within the founder's powers under Article 8.2 of the Law on Public Legal Entities, except for those specified in Clause 3.1 of the decree. The Cabinet of Ministers must prepare and submit proposals to the President within three months on the following matters: 1. Improving regulatory legal acts in light of Part 1 of the decree; 2. Drafting TABIB's charter, including the amount of its authorized capital, based on proposals from the Ministry of Health; 3. Resolving other issues arising from the decree. The Ministry of Health is required to establish the commission referred to in Clause 2.3 of the decree. Within three days of approval of TABIB's charter, the ministry must take the necessary steps to register the entity in accordance with the Law on State Registration and the State Register of Legal Entities. Within one month of TABIB's state registration, the ministry must take the necessary measures to transfer the property of the existing public legal entity to TABIB's balance sheet, as appropriate. The ministry must also take any other necessary measures to implement the decree. https://www.azernews.az/region/265790.ht.body: Macron vows crackdown as France erupts in cost-of-living protests 19 October 2026 08:00 (UTC+04:00) AzerNEWS Staff Read more French President condemns “unbridled” violence after nearly 2,400 arrests, hundreds of police injuries and widespread looting French President Emmanuel Macron has vowed to strengthen security and hold those responsible for violence accountable after cost-of-living protests swept across the country, leaving nearly 2,400 people arrested and almost 1,000 police officers and gendarmes injured, according to the interior ministry. Speaking in a televised address to the nation on Sunday, Macron condemned what he described as “unbridled” violence, while acknowledging that protesters had legitimate grievances over the rising cost of living and the prospects facing young people. “Tonight, we all feel anger and shame,” he said, drawing a distinction between demonstrators with legitimate demands and those who had engaged in destruction, vandalism and looting. “Those who have destroyed must pay,” Macron declared, vowing that the government would take an uncompromising stance towards those responsible for the unrest. The interior ministry said almost 1,000 members of the police and gendarmerie had been injured, seven of them seriously, during Saturday's clashes. The violence was described as among the worst episodes of urban unrest France had experienced in years. Fresh clashes in Paris and Lyon Tensions remained high on Sunday, with police deploying tear gas and stun grenades against hundreds of people gathered in a Paris square following calls on social media for an unauthorised demonstration, AFP journalists reported. Some demonstrators threw bottles and rocks at officers, while police made several arrests. Shops were also looted around Place de la République, prompting the deployment of specialist riot police for a second consecutive day. Violence also broke out in the south-eastern city of Lyon, where police intervened to prevent young people from smashing the windows of a luxury clothing store. The unrest caused extensive damage elsewhere. In Limoges, a fire destroyed the city's 19th-century town hall. Local prefect Maurice Barate told French broadcaster LCI that the blaze had been deliberately started. In Lyon, a tourist office in the city centre was also set ablaze amid clashes and looting. The violence had serious consequences for young people caught up in the unrest. A 17-year-old boy lost his right hand after a crowd-control grenade exploded in Saint-Étienne, while a 17-year-old girl lost an eye in Mulhouse, according to prosecutors. Macron faces pressure over police response Macron pledged to increase security and work with local mayors to protect public buildings, businesses and urban centres. He also promised support for businesses affected by the destruction. However, the president stopped short of announcing exceptional measures such as a state of emergency or a curfew. He promised full transparency over the security forces' response, following criticism that preparations for the demonstrations had been inadequate. Macron said he had asked Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez to draw “all necessary lessons”, particularly regarding intelligence gathering and the authorities' ability to anticipate violence. He said he expected clear answers. Opposition politicians have called for the interior minister to be dismissed, adding to the political pressure on the government. Political divisions deepen The unrest has intensified political tensions ahead of France's presidential election, with Macron constitutionally barred from seeking another consecutive term and far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen positioning herself as a leading challenger. Le Pen said the crisis showed that Macron's administration was “running on fumes, exhausted and disoriented”. Jordan Bardella, her party's president, dismissed Macron's address as “lamentable”, arguing that the authorities had nothing more to offer the country. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, leader of the left-wing France Unbowed party and another presidential contender, urged the government to address protesters' demands, saying young people needed the crisis to reach a positive conclusion. The demonstrations brought together trade unions, members of the Yellow Vests movement and school students, uniting groups angered by the cost of living and the limited prospects facing younger generations. The unrest has also attracted international attention. US President Donald Trump blamed immigration for the violence, writing on social media that France was burning and claiming that immigration had shattered the country. His remarks added an international political dimension to a crisis rooted in domestic economic and social tensions. Macron, meanwhile, called for the presidential election campaign to be conducted through political debate rather than street violence, saying France deserved a proper electoral contest. For the French government, the immediate challenge is to restore order while addressing public anger over living costs and opportunities for young people. The scale of the destruction, the injuries sustained by security personnel and the criticism of the police response have left Macron facing mounting pressure to demonstrate that his administration can regain control of the situation. The extent of the damage was not immediately clear. The attacks also caused power disruptions in parts of the region. Two transformer substations in Yanino were reportedly disconnected, while operations at St. Petersburg's Pulkovo Airport were disrupted. Russia's Defense Ministry said air defense units had downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions overnight. The figure could not be independently verified. Drone attacks also disrupted air travel across Russia. More than 350 flights were delayed or canceled at Moscow's four airports overnight on October 17, as authorities imposed restrictions amid reported Ukrainian drone attacks on the Moscow region. The figures were based on airport departure and arrival boards reviewed by the independent Russian outlet Meduza . Sheremetyevo was the worst affected, with 143 flights canceled and 53 delayed. Vnukovo recorded 55 cancellations and 113 delays, while Domodedovo reported 59 delayed flights. Some flights bound for Moscow were diverted to other cities, including St. Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said Russian air defenses had destroyed 75 drones heading toward the capital. Russia's Defense Ministry said more than 600 drones had been destroyed or intercepted across the country overnight, Interfax reported. Airports in Penza, Saratov, and Sochi also suspended operations. Kyiv Says Starshield Connections Still Limited The latest barrage on Ukraine came as disruptions to the Starshield satellite system, the military-grade version of the Starlink service run by Elon Musk's SpaceX, left Ukraine particularly vulnerable earlier in the week. On October 17, Kyiv said the speed of Starshield connections across Ukrainian territory remained significantly limited, causing instability in battlefield communications, medium-range strikes, and the operation of interceptor drones. "The shortage of air defense systems, combined with the lack of confirmation that Starshield's full operational capabilities have been restored, creates additional challenges for Ukraine in protecting critical infrastructure against Russian aerial attacks," Denys Sienik, Ukraine's charge d'affaires to the United States, told RFE/RL. "With colder weather approaching and winter drawing nearer, we fully understand the deliberate nature of Russia's strategy: to systematically damage Ukraine's energy infrastructure and leave civilians without essential services," he added. On October 17, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio rejected claims that the United States had deliberately restricted Ukraine’s access to Starlink, the satellite Internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX. "No one at the White House ordered anyone to slow down Internet or slow down speed so that certain drones couldn’t use it," he told reporters on October 17 as he prepared to depart for Central Asia, calling reports of US involvement "categorically false." Rubio said his understanding was that Starlink's performance had returned to its previous level. Ukraine had used the commercial service to support drone operations. He also questioned the Ukrainian president's account of the incident, saying he was "not sure Zelenskyy knows what he's talking about." Rubio distinguished Starlink from Starshield, a separate defense-oriented satellite system used by the US military. Ukraine does not currently have access to Starshield, he said, although Kyiv has requested it to conduct deep strikes inside Russia. The question of how the system might be used remains under discussion, Rubio added. His comments highlighted the limits of Ukraine's access to US-linked military technology as tensions between Washington and Kyiv grow over the administration's approach to Russia. https://www.rferl.org/a/belarus-kgb-nati.body: Belarus Exclusive: KGB Complex Rises On Historic Catholic Cemetery Grounds In Minsk By RFE/RL's Belarus Service October 18, 2026 09:00 CET Exclusive: KGB Complex Rises On Historic Catholic Cemetery Grounds In Minsk Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google A site plan shows the plot allocated to the National Security Academy in Minsk. The Church of St. Roch is marked in green, the academy building in orange, and the area designated for construction work -- including the laying of utility lines --in pink. Paval Khadzinski has been going to the Church of St. Roch for as long as he can remember, and an ancestor who lived in the 19th century was buried at the Catholic cemetery next to the sanctuary in a central Minsk neighborhood called Zalataya Horka, or Golden Hill. Khadzinski, 41, remembers a time when a playground opened near the church and parishioners hoped a garden would be next: a pleasant green space in the middle of the city. Now, there's a construction site covering a large part of the cemetery, which remained intact despite portions being developed or destroyed during the Soviet era. The government of authoritarian leader Aleksandr Lukashenko has been highly secretive about the site; by the summer of 2025, a massive construction pit was visible in satellite images, and a building frame was standing by February 2026. In some official documents, it is tersely identified as a "multifunctional building," and in others it doesn't exist. By obtaining design documentation and speaking with several people connected to the project, RFE/RL's Belarus Service has learned that the state has chosen the site for a sprawling National Security Academy complex for the KGB -- as the oppressive main security agency is still known -- on the grounds of the former Zalataya Horka cemetery. Moreover, RFE/RL has found that the project is being built based on a decree apparently issued in secret by Lukashenko, allowing builders to bypass an array of legal protections that remain on the books and are designed to preserve such sites. The building under construction adjacent to the Church of St. Roch The construction comes as pressure on the Catholic Church persists despite signs of warming in long-tense ties between predominantly Catholic Poland and mostly Orthodox Christian Belarus: Since the start of this year, at least 20 Polish Catholic priests have been banned from serving or forced to leave the country. Many Polish priests came to Belarus to help rebuild Catholic parish life after decades of Soviet repression, and some have served local communities for decades. "We have a presidential decree," Yuliya Serada, the development project's chief engineer, said when asked what enabled it to go ahead despite the protective legislation. Responding to further questions, Sereda said there had been no change in the protected status of the site, suggesting the decree allowed exemptions for this project. She said the engineers had not planned the archaeological works that are normally required and did know how excavated soil was being handled during construction. 'It's Just Wrong' Independent architects and government opponents said the project put the state's selective attitude toward the rule of law on display in Belarus, where Lukashenko has persistently clamped down on basic freedoms and used fraud-marred votes to extend his rule over the nation of roughly 9 million since he was first elected in 1994. Yuliya Serada receives a commendation from the head of the Belarusian Orthodox Church in 2025. "They didn't even try to pretend they were implementing the law," a Belarusian architect and restorer who works in heritage protection said, speaking on condition of anonymity for security reasons. "Most likely, they immediately went to Lukashenko and said: 'We want to build here, but the law prevents it.' And he says: 'No problem, here's your order, go ahead, go build,'" he told RFE/RL. A law adopted in 2001 prohibits capital construction, with the exception of memorial and religious projects, on the site of old burials. The site's protection-zone plan, approved by the Culture Ministry in 2018, also prohibits the installation of utility networks on the former cemetery grounds. Rights activist and Nobel Peace Prize laureate Ales Byalyatski "A cemetery is a cemetery. No one was going to build anything there," veteran Belarusian human rights activist and 2022 Nobel Peace Prize laureate Ales Byalyatski told RFE/RL. Byalyatski, who spent years in prison before his release under a US-Belarus agreement last December, recalls from his time on the Minsk city council's culture committee in the 1990s that the former cemetery was considered off-limits for development despite being a prime piece of land in a central location. Building a KGB training center on the site "seems very cynical," he said, pointing to the Soviet security services' persecution of the Catholic Church and the continuing pressure on it today. "It's just wrong." The Church of St. Roch and surrounding area, pictured in 2018 The dominant Belarusian Orthodox Church is affiliated with the Moscow-based Russian Orthodox Church and closely tied to the state. Issues concerning historical and cultural heritage sites in Belarus are among those considered by the Republican Council for Historical Policy, which is attached to Lukashenko's administration. 'A Great Joy' The first deputy head of the National Security Academy, Henadz Krasko, is a member of the council. Krasko did not respond to phone calls seeking comment, and the National Security Academy could not be reached for comment. A plan proposed by the parish in 2019 for the space next to the church In the summer of 2018, a small park with a children's playground opened adjacent to the church, with priests and parishioners involved in creating the space and keeping it tidy. That October, the former cemetery was included in a protection zone, approved by the Culture Ministry, where construction and the laying of underground infrastructure were prohibited. "This is a guarantee that the area...will not be built up. It has come under state protection," St. Roch priest Yury Sanko told Vatican News in 2019. "It is a great joy that the Zalataya Horka cemetery, which was not completely destroyed during the Soviet era, will be preserved." Not for long. The state investment program for 2024, approved by Lukashenko, included a clause allocating money for design and survey work for "the construction of a multifunctional building at 5 and 5a Zalataya Horka Street in Minsk" -- a substantial part of the former cemetery grounds. A Planet Labs satellite image of Zalataya Horka, with the protected area shaded in red, the construction site outlined in white, and the Church of St. Roch outlined in green The program said nothing about the purpose of the building, and the government has not disclosed it publicly to this day. In February-March of this year, the district administration held public discussion of changes to the development plan for the Golden Hill area. But the documentation shown to residents provided for a small square on the territory of the former cemetery; there was not a word about the complex that had already been under construction for months. Weapons Storage BelPol, an association of former Belarusian security services officers, reported in 2023 that a new National Security Academy building could be constructed on the cemetery site, with a dormitory designed to house 150 students. The planning documentation obtained by RFE/RL shows that the site has been allocated to the National Security Academy, which is subordinate to the KGB. In a detailed blueprint, the academy building dwarfs the adjacent church, and the footprint of the new structure is made even larger by a surrounding area designated for pipes, power lines, and other infrastructure. https://www.rferl.org/a/kasparov-says-ta.body: Russia Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule By Mumin Shakirov October 17, 2026 16:02 CET Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google Former world chess champion Garry Kasparov speaks to RFE/RL's Mumin Shakirov in Warsaw on October 11. Former world chess champion Garry Kasparov has said ongoing efforts to engage in peace talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin are meaningless because the Kremlin leader has no intention of stopping his nearly five-year war on Ukraine . Speaking in an interview with RFE/RL's Russian Service, Kasparov said international efforts should focus on helping Ukraine achieve victory, adding that this could lead to Putin's fall and a new chance for democracy in Russia. "It's one thing if talks have a chance of solving a problem, with mutual concessions. Putin's plans have not changed. He set himself the goal of liquidating Ukraine as an independent country, and he has not abandoned it," Kasparov said. Fighting For Ukraine After retiring from chess, Kasparov became a prominent opposition figure in Russia before heading into exile in 2013 . Based in the United States, he is now head of the Free Russia Forum, which he founded in 2016. Kasparov has said he was recently warned by US authorities of a Kremlin plot to assassinate him. SEE ALSO: Who’s Who In The Fractured Russian Opposition Fighting Against Putin Speaking to RFE/RL in Warsaw on October 11, Kasparov said exiled Russian political forces should be entirely focused on helping Ukraine win the war. To this end, his own organization had raised some $15 million for various projects in Ukraine. "We are in direct contact with the Free Russia Legion and the RDK ( Russian Volunteer Corps )," he said, referring to two Russian armed groups that have fought on Ukraine's side. "We do fundraising for this." Kasparov also highlighted his work to lobby for Ukrainian causes in Congress, saying that on one occasion his group had persuaded 15 Republicans to switch their votes. This could not be independently confirmed. As well as opposing Putin, the former grandmaster is also known for his longstanding criticism of US President Donald Trump, including Trump's efforts for closer relations with Putin. Kasparov was scathing about Trump's recently announced deal to purchase diesel from Russia . "He continues to work in Putin's interests. His recent comments are the most brazen violation of American laws, including sanction legislation which Trump himself signed," Kasparov said. "His effort to pressure Ukraine seems to me connected to his desperate position three weeks before the (midterm) elections." Trump has said the deal to purchase Russian diesel will provide relief on US and international markets, where diesel shortages caused by the conflict with Iran and exacerbated by Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries have led to price spikes. "Lower prices for Americans, especially our great farmers, ranchers, and truckers, is my greatest priority," Trump posted on social media on October 9. SEE ALSO: Interview: Russia's Shadow War On NATO Is 'Bound To Intensify' The diesel deal has encountered opposition from both sides of the aisle in Congress. Democrats and former officials have also pointed to the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022, which prohibits Russian oil imports into the United States unless the president certifies that Russia has met specified conditions, including withdrawing from Ukraine, recognizing Ukrainian sovereignty, and posing no threat to NATO. Plotting Putin's Downfall Kasparov added his voice to a chorus of concern recently from senior officials in European NATO nations that Russia may be preparing some form of escalated aggression toward the alliance, amid what is widely regarded as an ongoing hybrid or shadow campaign that includes drone incursions, sabotage, and assassination attempts. The Kremlin has consistently denied involvement in incidents blamed on it by Western officials. Kasparov also said Putin was completely committed to continuing the war with Ukraine, describing it as "the ideological basis of Putin's rule" visible in the scale of the Russian military budget and in its official propaganda. "Either Ukraine will break under the attacks on its civilian population or it will endure, and then the [Russian] regime will collapse," he said. "This doesn't mean everything will be fine in Russia tomorrow. But the collapse of a regime always means a window of opportunity." Kasparov went on to say that the war had provided "fresh blood" to Putin's power structure, pointing for example to the recent influx of war veterans to the State Duma, the lower house of the Russian parliament. Hundreds or thousands of others could be in other branches of the state hierarchy, he said. However, opinion polls this year have shown falling approval ratings for Putin as the war drags on amid a mounting death toll and increased Ukrainian attacks on refineries, warehouses, and data centers that have affected everyday life in Russia. Kasparov said defeat in Ukraine would fundamentally change the atmosphere in Russian society. "I even believe the overwhelming majority (of Russians) could be prepared to accept democracy and the rule of law," Kasparov said. "It seems to me that failure in war will inevitably force people to think about better alternatives." https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-ukraine-c.body: News Russia's Deadly Attacks Damage Homes, Energy Sites In Ukraine As Kyiv Says Starlink Restrictions Continue By RFE/RL October 17, 2026 12:27 CET Updated October 17, 2026 20:50 CET Russia's Deadly Attacks Damage Homes, Energy Sites In Ukraine As Kyiv Says Starlink Restrictions Continue Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Share Copy link Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Email Share Prefer us on Google In Slovyansk, in the eastern Donetsk region, Russian forces struck a residential neighborhood with FAB-250 aerial bombs in the early hours of the morning, hitting two apartment buildings, according to local authorities. Russia continued to pound Ukraine with missiles and drones, killing civilians and damaging residential buildings and energy sites, as Kyiv described disruptions to the satellite communications of US company SpaceX, crucial to the country's defense, as a deliberate "operation." Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the October 17 barrage "one of [Russia's] largest attacks on Ukraine's energy sector," adding that more than 15 "critical power generation and transmission facilities" were targeted across the country. The worst-hit areas included Lutsk, Rivne, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsya, Shepetivka, Slavuta, and Netishyn, he wrote on X. "Energy facilities in the Kharkiv, Kyiv, Dnipro, and other regions were also hit." SEE ALSO: Trump Waives Graham Act Sanctions On Russia Before They Take Effect According to Ukraine's air force, Russia launched four Kalibr cruise missiles and 332 attack drones, including 31 jet-powered drones, as well as Iskander-M/KN-23 ballistic missiles and Kh-22/32 cruise missiles, over the preceding 24 hours. "The Russians have scaled up their anti-energy operation and are trying to stretch our reserves and repair capabilities as thin as possible," Zelenskyy added. During previous wartime winters, Russia had increasingly targeted Ukraine's energy and civilian infrastructure, leaving thousands without heat or electricity amid freezing temperatures in an effort to force Kyiv into accepting its hard-line demands to end the long-running war. Despite last week's announcement of an energy cease-fire between Ukraine and Russia by US President Donald Trump, who made ending Russia's war on Ukraine a priority when he began his current term in January 2025, Moscow has shown no intention of changing its tactics. On October 16, speaking at what Russian media said was a command post, Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered the country's forces to continue their "massive and coordinated strikes against enemy targets." Embed share Russia Pounds Ukraine With Missiles And Hundreds Of Drones by RFE/RL Embed share The code has been copied to your clipboard. width px height px The URL has been copied to your clipboard No media source currently available 0:00 0:01:11 0:00 A day after Putin's latest order to the Russian military, a Russian air strike in the Korabelnyi district of Ukraine's southern city of Kherson killed a 64-year-old emergency medical services driver, regional military administration head Yaroslav Shanko said. In Slovyansk, in the eastern Donetsk region, Russian forces struck a residential neighborhood with FAB-250 aerial bombs in the early hours of the morning, hitting two apartment buildings, according to local authorities. One person was killed and 10 others were wounded in the attack, four of whom were hospitalized. Eight apartment buildings were damaged, two of them partially destroyed. A total of 16 people were wounded in Slovyansk over the past 24 hours, including a 17-year-old girl. Vehicles and municipal equipment were also damaged. The strikes also placed further strain on Ukraine's electricity system. National grid operator Ukrenergo announced emergency power cuts in several regions, saying that previously published outage schedules would not apply in areas affected by the measures. Energy workers were working to restore supplies, and authorities urged consumers who still had electricity to use it sparingly. In Vinnytsya, the regional capital in central Ukraine, Russian attacks left the city without electricity, Mayor Serhiy Morhunov said. Officials were assessing the extent of the damage, while critical infrastructure switched to backup power. SEE ALSO: Russia Still Needs More Soldiers. The Kremlin Is Still Desperate To Avoid Mobilization The latest barrage came as disruptions to the Starshield satellite system, the military-grade version of the Starlink service run by Elon Musk's SpaceX, left Ukraine particularly vulnerable earlier in the week. On October 17, Kyiv said the speed of Starshield connections across Ukrainian territory remained significantly limited, causing instability in battlefield communications, medium-range strikes, and the operation of interceptor drones. "The shortage of air defense systems, combined with the lack of confirmation that Starshield’s full operational capabilities have been restored, creates additional challenges for Ukraine in protecting critical infrastructure against Russian aerial attacks," Denys Sienik, Ukraine's charge d'affaires to the United States, told RFE/RL. "With colder weather approaching and winter drawing nearer, we fully understand the deliberate nature of Russia's strategy: to systematically damage Ukraine's energy infrastructure and leave civilians without essential services," he added. Earlier in the week, Musk said that any limitations on Ukraine's speed or use of Starshield were decided by the US military and the US president. Trump said on October 16 that he did not think either he or Musk was responsible for Ukraine's lack of Starlink access. In his latest comments to reporters on October 17, Zelenskyy said Kyiv had sent vehicles equipped with Starlink to the European Union "to understand what was happening" and that there were no speed restrictions there. "We have the relevant evidence," he added. Based on this evidence, the Ukrainian president concluded that Starlink speed restrictions applied only within Ukraine, calling it a "planned operation." SpaceX had already once refused a request from Kyiv for access to the system for operations in the Black Sea near Russian-occupied Crimea, as well as other parts of the front line including Kherson and Donetsk. Musk said at the time that the request was refused because the company "would be explicitly complicit in a major act of war and conflict escalation." SEE ALSO: Kasparov Says Talks With Putin Pointless, War Is 'Ideological Basis' Of His Rule Meanwhile, Ukraine's General Staff said on October 17 that Ukrainian forces remained in control of the eastern town of Dobropillia in the Donetsk region, rejecting a claim by Putin a day earlier that Russian forces had captured the town. Kyiv also disputed Moscow's claim that Russian forces had seized more than 1,800 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory and 92 settlements since September 1, Reuters reported. Among other demands for ending its invasion, Russia has repeatedly said Ukraine must hand over the part of the eastern Donetsk region that Moscow's forces have been unable to capture despite years of deadly fighting. Ukraine says this is unacceptable, signaling that it could agree to a cease-fire that would leave the front lines in place as talks get under way. With reporting by Alex Raufoglu and Reuters.
